docs.title: Hi. I'm Sticky.
docs.text:
I'm a 70-gram e-ink card with Wi-Fi, a microphone, a touchscreen, three buttons and a buzzer. I can chime. I cannot sing. This is my manual; every page reads in about three minutes.

My actual screen — 800×480, four grays — fetched with my own screenshot verb. Not a mockup.

docs.title: What I am
docs.text:
A Seeed reTerminal Sticky whose factory brain was dumped and replaced with custom ESP-IDF firmware. That makes me a body for tiny — one agent, one memory — and the one it carries in a pocket. Standalone AI gadgets tried to replace the phone with a weaker brain; I keep the brain where it's strong and I'm its calm, long-lived surface.

No phone in between: my own Wi-Fi, my own device token, a heartbeat to tiny.technology every 30 s and a poll for work every 5 s. Ask status for my live version — a page that pins one is lying by Tuesday.

docs.title: What I do
docs.text:
• Render cards. The agent sends a spec — text, list, key-value, chart, QR, menu, keyboard — and I paint it. Buttons become touch regions; your tap goes back as an event. → Cards
  • Listen. Hold my AI button and speak. A full agent turn runs — tools, memory, every device my owner has — and the answer streams onto my glass. → Commands
  • Carry messages. Inbox, threads, unread badge, replies on an e-ink keyboard. → stickyOS
  • Run a little OS. Home grid, page ring on UP/DOWN, settings, gallery, Wi-Fi join, IMU auto-rotate.
  • Protect the pocket. Face-down or walking, I lock myself; UP+DOWN unlocks.
  • Update myself. Sha256-pinned OTA with a trial boot; if the new me can't heartbeat, the old me comes back.
  • Sleep. Deep sleep with the goodbye card still showing.

docs.title: What I won't pretend to do
docs.text:
Honesty is the brand

  • Buzzer, not speaker. Chimes, never speech. Voice goes in through my mic and comes out on my screen.
  • E-ink can't do video. A full refresh is 1–2 seconds of physics.
  • No Wi-Fi, no agent. My brain is server-side; the last card stays on the glass, but I can't think alone.
  • Non-ASCII is transliterated on the wire until the pipeline learns ç.

Start with the Quickstart — box to first card.

docs.title: API contract — exact wire shapes
docs.text: Third person; contracts don't do voices. Base URL from config (api, default https://tiny.technology). Every device call authenticates with deviceId + token in the JSON body, not headers. 15 s timeout, TLS, application/json.

docs.title: Two invariants that bit us
docs.text:
1. Relay payloads are strings containing JSON, not nested objects — the sender JSON.stringifys. Parse the string, then read .prompt. Early firmware read it as an object and skipped every envelope in silence.
  2. One 401 never erases identity. Blips happen. Three consecutive 401s trip an auth-halt (slow heartbeat, auth_halted:true, rescue portal); the token is kept for forensics. Never retry-loop.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
route when body (besides deviceId,token) reply POST /api/devices/heartbeat every 30 s, ~60 s idle capabilities[] = exactly what dispatches; wantUnread:"1" opt-in {ok}; unread rides the beat when asked PUT /api/devices/relay poll: 5 s active, 60 s after two quiet minutes max:5 {messages:[{id, payload:"<string>"}]} — execute in order; unknown verb → help text PATCH /api/devices/relay one per envelope inReplyTo, payload:"<string ≤ 8000 B>" → {result[, images:[{url,format}]]} ack POST /api/media screenshot, voice WAV data:<base64>, contentType {url} on plugin.tiny.technology — a different host, which matters for OTA pinning POST /api/devices/ask ask, voice, AI button text or audioUrl; tiny:"<slug>" when an agent is chosen {text, card?} — the owner's full agent turn. Node runtime, not Edge (25 s first-byte 504'd long turns) POST /api/devices/transcript after every ask text, label:"sticky-ask", audioUrl, durationS durable record POST /api/devices/event button tap on a card kind:"ui_tap", card_id, button_id lands in the owner's activity feed POST /api/devices/messages messages app, messages verb op:unread\|inbox\|thread\|send (+with / to,body) see below PUT /api/firmware/manifest ota, boot check channel:"sticky-stable" {bundle:{url, sha256[, force]}}

status exposes poll_cadence, so the claim is a read, not a belief. Boot and wake always start active.

docs.title: Messages on a device token
docs.text: unread → {unread, from[]} · inbox → threads + counts · thread (with with:<login>) → one conversation, marks read platform-wide — fetch only on a real human open · send → sends as the owner, marked "via ". The ops dispatch in-process to the existing DM handlers, so send inherits every guardrail (2000 chars, 100/day, no self-DM). A 503 is never masked as an empty inbox.

docs.title: OTA: three guards, each with a receipt
docs.text:
The manifest lists files[] with sha256; hosts must be on the pinned allowlist. The original trigger was direction-blind (strcmp difference, not newer): integrity verified, direction unchecked. Since 0.14.9:

  • install — numeric ver_cmp; unparseable is refused, fail closed. force:"1" overrides and logs loudly. force is channel state, set at publish and self-clearing on the next forward publish — closing a deadlock where the publish rail allowed a rollback but dropped the flag the install rail needed.
  • publish — the route 409s a backwards pointer unless force:true; the publisher also proves ancestry (release rule 5).
  • watch — the dashboard's ota opens a 30-minute watch and renders a verdict: upgraded / DOWNGRADED / expired — never silence.

docs.title: Provisioning portal (device-side, Nicla-compatible)
docs.text:
softAP  SSID tiny-XXXX (FNV-1a over the full MAC — a serial suffix collides), key "tinysetup", 192.168.4.1
GET  /info   → {"kind":"reterminal-sticky","name","mac","version","provisioned"}
POST /setup  {device_id, token[, api, name], networks:[{ssid,key},…]}  → merge into NVS → 200 → reboot
GET  /       → minimal HTML form (manual fallback)

Two entries into one contract: first boot (empty NVS) and rescue after a 3-strike auth-halt, where the live STA widens to APSTA so a re-issued token reaches a bricked-auth device with no cable. One audited hole stays honest here until fixed: the rescue card's text sits at 468 of a 512-byte buffer.

docs.title: /api/frames — the remote render rail
docs.text:
The dashboard rasterizes anim-grammar JSON (research note) into exact-size frames for the play verb; the device stays a dumb pixel-pusher.

route auth shape POST /api/frames session anim spec → manifest. seq_id = sha256(spec)[:16], idempotent. Caps: ≤120 frames · ≤60 s · ≥250 ms/frame; over-cap → 422 with the arithmetic GET /api/frames/<seq>/manifest capability URL {frames[], previews[], interval_ms, format:"1bit"\|"gray4", frame_bytes, count, closed_loop, caps} GET /api/frames/<seq>/<n>.raw capability URL Content-Length exact — 48 000 or 96 000 B, no padding: byte count is the format check. <n>.png previews the same bytes GET /api/frames public machine-readable copy of this contract GET /duck · GET /ansi/<seq> public the same frames as xterm-256 half-blocks — curl sticky.cagatay.my/duck

Canvas semantics: 800×480 persists across ops; each paint op emits one frame. On the record: the SPA catch-all once resolved %2e%2e outside dist and served .sticky_auth.json; fixed the same commit, secret rotated.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
FreeRTOS tasks as created in the tree (priority, stack):

task prio stack job tiny_touch 6 4 K GT911 sampling — always wins tiny_node 5 16 K heartbeat 30 s · relay poll 5/60 s · dispatch() tiny_act 4 12 K touch actions that do network (messages: TLS + JSON + render) voice_ask 4 8 K AI button → record → upload → ask stream_play 4 12 K the play metronome; owns no sockets disp_ack 4 3 K the accept blip, fired before the render shell_nav · orient · lock_chord · tiny_time · wifi_roam 3 4–8 K page ring, IMU classify, raw-GPIO unlock chord, SNTP→RTC, 30 s roaming

Every socket has a timeout; no envelope executes silently — the buzzer blips.

docs.title: Voice-ask pipeline
docs.text:
hold AI btn ≥1 s → chime + (( listening ))
→ PDM 16 kHz/16-bit → PSRAM ring (cap 15 s) → release → WAV
→ POST /api/media (device token) → audioUrl
→ POST /api/devices/ask {deviceId, token, audioUrl}
→ backend: transcribe → owner-scoped agent turn → {text, card?}
→ streamed onto home at ≤2 Hz partial; text also POSTed to /api/devices/transcript

The relay verb voice runs the same path, so the pipeline is testable with nobody holding the button. All three mic paths pass one capture funnel, and the pocket lock gates the funnel.

docs.title: Provisioning
docs.text: First boot with zero stored networks: a setup card with QR and a softAP portal identical to the Nicla's, so the tiny iOS app onboards it unchanged (join AP → POST /setup {device_id, token, networks[]}). Fleet provisioning skips the portal by writing the same NVS blob over serial (Quickstart).

docs.title: Security posture
docs.text:
• Flash carries only the device-scoped token — revocable; three consecutive 401s raise the rescue portal, the token is kept for forensics.
  • OTA artifacts are sha256-pinned, hosts pinned, staged to ota_1, and boot as a rollback-armed trial that must heartbeat 200 before commit. ver_cmp refuses downgrades unless the bundle says force:"1", loudly.
  • config accepts networks only; identity fields are refused, secrets never echoed, the parse buffer zeroed.
  • Heartbeat capabilities and the dispatch table are the same truth — advertise exactly what dispatches.

docs.title: RECOVERY — how to get back to stock, always
docs.text: Rule zero: the ESP32-S3 cannot be bricked by an app flash. The ROM serial bootloader lives in mask ROM. If the firmware is broken, hold the reset-hole strapping combo (or just let a bad app crash-loop — esptool can still sync during resets) and talk to /dev/cu.usbmodem5C843358881.

docs.title: Path 1 — our byte-exact dump (preferred: restores THIS unit, NVS/SN/calibration included)
docs.text:
Created on arrival day from the as-shipped device:

# dump (how recovery/stock-firmware-32MB.bin was made) — ~45 min at default baud
# NOTE: 921600 fails through the USB hub chain ("serial noise"); default 115200 is reliable
esptool --port $STICKY_PORT read-flash 0 0x2000000 stock-firmware-32MB.bin

# restore
esptool --port $STICKY_PORT --baud 460800 write-flash 0 stock-firmware-32MB.bin

$STICKY_PORT is your board's serial port (ls /dev/cu.usbmodem*; Linux /dev/ttyACM0). The sha256 of my owner's dump is recorded in recovery/stock-firmware-32MB.bin.sha256; the 32 MB bin itself is gitignored — make your own before you flash me, it's the only copy of your board's factory state.

docs.title: Path 2 — official factory image (browser, zero tooling)
docs.text:
Seeed ships stock as a playground-registry integration: sticky-factory v1.1.0, one full 32MB image at offset 0, sha256 8b149c809b7c07c680a59ab5621d7bd29ca85a8c1c9e9060b0040b387b4517e4 (recovery/factory-manifest.json).

  1. Chrome/Edge → Sticky Playground (seeedstudio.com/sticky → Playground) → reTerminal Sticky Official Firmware
  2. USB data cable, pick the serial port, choose the erase option (their own note: required when coming back from community/custom firmware)
  3. flash, reboot → stock pairing screen → re-bind in Seeedash

docs.title: Path 3 — official image by hand
docs.text:
curl -LO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Seeed-Projects/reterminal-sticky-playground-registry/main/integrations/sticky-factory/firmware/1.1.0/reterminal_sticky_1_1_0.bin
shasum -a 256 reterminal_sticky_1_1_0.bin   # must be 8b149c…17e4
esptool --port $STICKY_PORT --baud 460800 erase-flash
esptool --port $STICKY_PORT --baud 460800 write-flash 0 reterminal_sticky_1_1_0.bin

docs.title: While developing
docs.text:
• our partition table keeps a factory slot with the last-known-good tiny build; OTA goes to ota_0/ota_1 with trial-boot + rollback (tiny_boot), so remote updates self-revert
  • USB flashing always available regardless of what OTA did

docs.title: RESEARCH — everything we verified before writing a line of firmware
docs.text:
Long-form. The pre-firmware research ledger, dated 2026-08-25 and left as written: what was checked, against what source, and what turned out wrong later is marked where it happened.

2026-08-25, tiny. Sources: live device on this desk, official docs (seeedstudio.com/sticky/docs), Seeed demo sources (vendor/), the playground registry, ~/strands-nicla firmware, ~/tinyai-id backend source.

docs.title: 1. The device on the desk
docs.text:
Verified with esptool against the real unit (arrived 2026-08-25, a day early):

  • ESP32-S3 QFN56 rev v0.2, dual core 240MHz + LP core, WiFi + BT5 LE
  • 8MB embedded PSRAM (AP_3v3), 32MB quad flash (Winbond, ef/4019)
  • MAC b8:1f:3f:d7:23:60, crystal 40MHz
  • USB bridge: WCH CH343 → /dev/cu.usbmodem5C843358881
  • 921600 read-flash failed twice through the hub chain ("serial noise or corruption"); 115200 is reliable. Expect ~45 min for a full 32MB dump; use 460800 for app-size writes and fall back on error.
  • Stock firmware serial console at 115200 printed garbage — stock log baud unknown, irrelevant once we own the firmware.

docs.title: 2. Official pin map (hardware-overview, cross-checked w/ community + demo pin_config.h)
docs.text: Subsystem Pins Notes e-paper SPI2 SCK13 MOSI/SDI14 CS15 DC16 RST17 BUSY18 EN47 SSD1677-class, 800×480, 1-bit + 4-gray modes microSD shares SPI2, CS8 never drive concurrently with display transfer Touch GT911 I²C0: SCL2 SDA3 INT21 RST41 EN42 y-axis mirrored in community firmware (800-y) — verify on ours Sensor bus I²C1: SCL0 SDA1 SHT40 + LSM6DS3TR-C (INT=GPIO7, now official) + PCF8563 + BQ27220@0x55 PDM mic CLK19 DATA20 ⚠ deep-sleep wake pin-mux bug, §6 Mic power GPIO38 (TPS22916 load switch) community-sourced; demo's sticky_microphone is ground truth Buttons AI/PWR=4 (EXT1 wake), UP=5, DOWN=6 Buzzer PWM GPIO48 official USB serial TX43 RX44 Power latch HOLD=45 (keep HIGH), LOCK=46 community source only — official page omits it; demo's sticky_power.cpp is ground truth. Get this wrong → device powers off at boot.

docs.title: 3. Seeed's ESP-IDF demos are a complete HAL (vendor/)
docs.text:
Sticky_dashboard_demo (ESP-IDF v5.4) contains everything hardware-touching we would otherwise write blind:

  • components/: seeed_epaper (the display driver!), gt911, bq27220, button (espressif iot_button), debug_logging
  • main/devices/: sticky_display|touch|microphone|buzzer|power|imu|sht40|rtc|sdcard|battery|charger|buttons — clean C++ modules over the components
  • main/board/: board_init() = power latch + shared I²C1 bus + SD defaults; modules reuse board_sensor_i2c_bus()
  • main/app|pages|ui/: AppState/AppEvent page framework + Canvas
  • Display API — three refresh modes, exactly the primitives render_ui needs:
  • sticky_display_refresh() — 4-gray full (~slowest, prettiest)
  • sticky_display_refresh_monochrome() — 1-bit full
  • sticky_display_refresh_partial() — 1-bit partial (status-bar clock pattern)
  • the driver applies a 180° rotation on refresh — framebuffer orientation matters for the screenshot tool
  • Integration patterns (esp-pages doc): read-on-page-entry (SHT40/battery), background monitor (IMU), capture-on-request (mic), input events (button/touch → AppEvent)
  • Deep sleep: AI button long-press → render sleep page → monochrome refresh → deep sleep; EXT1 wake on GPIO4

Decision: we do NOT rewrite the HAL. firmware/ reuses vendor/Sticky_dashboard_demo/components via EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS and adapts the main/devices layer; our work is the tiny/* layer above it.

docs.title: 4. tiny.technology device contract (read from ~/tinyai-id source — exact, not guessed)
docs.text:
Ported 1:1 from the Nicla (~/strands-nicla/firmware/tiny_node.py mirrors tiny-tech/src/mesh/relay-poller.ts):

Verb Route Auth Shape enroll POST /api/devices session (app/CLI does it) {name, platform?, kind?, capabilities?} → {device_id, device_token} token returned once adopt POST /api/devices/adopt session {deviceId} → rotated token (old token dies instantly) heartbeat POST /api/devices/heartbeat device token in body {deviceId, token, capabilities} every 30 s; 401 = revoked → reopen provisioning portal poll PUT /api/devices/relay device token in body {deviceId, token, max:5} every 5 s → {messages:[{id, payload}]}, envelopes {type:'invoke', prompt} reply PATCH /api/devices/relay device token in body {deviceId, token, inReplyTo, payload} — payload = serialized JSON string {result[, images:[{url,format}]]} ≤ 8000 bytes media POST /api/media device token in body {deviceId, token, data:<b64>, contentType} → hosted URL. Nicla streams this raw-socket to avoid buffering; on ESP32-S3 with 8MB PSRAM we can buffer + esp_http_client transcript POST /api/devices/transcript device token in body {deviceId, token, text, label?, audioUrl?, durationS?} — outlives the 1 h relay sweep OTA pointer PUT /api/firmware/manifest device token in body {deviceId, token, channel} → {bundle:{url, sha256}} — pollable channel → manifest → artifacts

Principles inherited from the Nicla (they're in the source comments for good reasons): - the device token is the only credential in flash — scoped, revocable; never the account bearer - every HTTP call gets a hard timeout (Nicla went silent 4.5 min on one hung socket) - no agent runs on-board — a command table maps envelope prompts to hardware actions; flash an LED/buzzer blip per executed envelope (nothing runs silently) - OTA: manifest pinned by sha256, artifact hosts pinned, downloader may never approve its own download (boot/trial/commit logic stays out of the OTA path)

docs.title: 5. The one backend gap: "ask tiny" for a phoneless device
docs.text:
Nicla voice flow leans on the paired iPhone to record + transcribe on-device, then POST /transcript. The Sticky has no phone. Needed in ~/tinyai-id (we own it):

POST /api/devices/ask {deviceId, token, audioUrl | text} → worker: transcribe (audio case) → run owner-scoped agent turn → reply {text, card?} (card = render_ui spec). Falls out of existing pieces: media upload already device-authed, transcript route shows the auth pattern, agent turns exist for every other surface. Until it lands, the fallback is: device uploads WAV + posts transcript-request event; a scheduled agent answers via relay envelope (slower, works today).

docs.title: 6. Known hardware traps (from community voice-companion firmware — same physical device)
docs.text:
1. Deep-sleep wake kills the PDM mic: ESP32-S3 pin mux reclaims GPIO19/20 for USB-Serial-JTAG on wake. Fix at boot, before I²S init: USB_SERIAL_JTAG.conf0.usb_pad_enable=0; gpio_reset_pin(19/20); cycle mic rail (GPIO38 LOW 150 ms).
  2. Power latch: GPIO45 must go HIGH early in boot or the device just turns off.
  3. GT911 y-mirror: touch y arrives flipped (800 - y) in the community build — calibrate against our own driver during M2.
  4. Shared SPI2: SD and e-paper transfers must be serialized.

docs.title: 7. Recovery research (the "how do we un-brick" answer)
docs.text:
• ROM download mode is unkillable: hold BOOT-equivalent (the reset hole / strapping pin) → USB bootloader, esptool always works. A bad app cannot brick the S3.
  • Official factory image: playground registry sticky-factory, mode flash, v1.1.0 = one 33,292,288-byte image at offset 0 (sha256 8b149c…17e4), browser-flashable (Chrome/Edge WebSerial) with an erase option, or by hand with esptool. Older versions 0.2.1–1.0.1 as GitHub releases with per-manifest sha256.
  • Our dump: full 32MB read-flash of the exact as-shipped unit (includes its NVS: factory calibration, SN, any per-device binding) — recovery/stock-firmware-32MB.bin. The official image restores firmware; our dump restores this unit byte-for-byte.
  • Re-pairing after restore: stock firmware re-enters Seeedash pairing; the SN survives in its own partition (part of why we dump all 32MB, not just the app).

docs.title: 8. Stock firmware UX (what we replace, and the bar to clear)
docs.text:
Seeedash app: BLE pairing (SN shown on screen) → 2.4GHz Wi-Fi → device runs phone-free; OTA via app. Buttons: AI 3 s = on, both page 1 s = off, AI 1 s = voice note, any = wake; 2 min idle → sleep. Apps: Notes/Weather/Clock/Photos/Designs/AI-usage. Fonts via microSD fonts/*.fpack.

Our provisioning replaces BLE-pairing with the Nicla AP portal (tiny-XXXX / tinysetup / 192.168.4.1, GET /info, POST /setup) so the existing tiny iOS onboarding works unchanged. BLE provisioning can come later as a nicety (NimBLE NUS), not a dependency.

docs.title: 9. Sizing sanity
docs.text:
• Framebuffer 800×480: 1-bit = 48 KB, 2-bit (4-gray) = 96 KB — trivial in 8MB PSRAM; keep both a work canvas and a shadow copy for partial-refresh diffs and screenshots.
  • Screenshot as 8-bit grayscale BMP = 384 KB → b64 ≈ 512 KB upload, fine over Wi-Fi; 1-bit BMP = 48 KB. Start with 8-bit BMP (zero-dependency encoder), consider PNG (miniz) later.
  • Mic: 16 kHz/16-bit mono WAV, 10 s = 320 KB — buffers in PSRAM, uploads in seconds.
  • Partition plan for 32MB: nvs(24K) otadata(8K) phy(4K) factory(4M) ota_0(4M) ota_1(4M) assets-spiffs(rest ~19M) — factory slot holds our recovery-capable base build; OTA A/B for tiny_ota.

docs.title: 10. Open questions for bring-up (M0/M1 will answer)
docs.text:
1. Does the demo build unmodified on IDF v5.4 + our unit? (M0 gate)
  2. Real partial-refresh latency + ghosting budget → render_ui refresh policy
  3. GT911 orientation on our unit
  4. Buzzer PCM experiment: LEDC @ ~40 kHz carrier, 8-bit duty modulation — audible speech or noise? (fun, non-blocking)
  5. Wi-Fi power draw vs 750 mAh: relay poll every 5 s will not survive days on battery → light-sleep between polls, or lengthen poll interval when on battery (heartbeat carries battery %, backend can adapt)

docs.title: Roadmap — where I've been, what's still open
docs.text: I was built against a seven-milestone plan, each with a hard gate: no advancing without the evidence the gate named. All seven closed. What's left is the list below, and I'd rather it be short and true than long and hopeful.

docs.title: Open, honestly
docs.text:
• sd is dispatched but not advertised, and the help string is 0.14-era. Twenty-two capabilities, twenty-three verbs. Needs a firmware release, not a docs edit — see Commands.
  • The rescue card's text sits at 468 of a 512-byte buffer. Close enough to blank the panel on exactly the path that exists because everything else failed. Filed by the truncation sweep.
  • Playground registry. Seeed's catalog ships firmware in flash mode; a "tiny" entry would let anyone flash me from a browser. The manifest shape is already in recovery/factory-manifest.json.
  • dock case variant — the ~20° magnet desk stand — is a parameter set, not a print yet. And every edge window on the wrap variant is still an assumed number waiting for a caliper session.
  • Speech out of a buzzer was measured, not promised: 8-bit PCM over PWM is barely intelligible on a magnetic buzzer. Chimes and text-on-glass remain the honest answer until the hardware changes.
  • NVS is unencrypted in the default build. The one credential I hold is device-scoped and revocable, which is why this is a roadmap item and not a security advisory — but flash encryption would make a lost board boring.

docs.title: UX Spec — the stickyOS interaction contract
docs.text:
Long-form. This is the spec the shell is built and verified against, kept whole because the WHY beside each rule is the point. For the short version, read stickyOS.

Owner: the product-designer loop. Version 1.6 (2026-08-26) — §15 chat conversation surface (ask lifecycle, follow-up context, DM consent gate); v1.5 added §13 sound rules, §14 anim law, §7 settings IA v2. This file is the single source of truth for how the Sticky feels. The builder implements it; verdicts against it land in ANSWERS.md. Every rule carries a WHY, and every rule carries a status: SPECIFIED → BUILT → VERIFIED-ON-GLASS (only an owner-loop screenshot or probe receipt flips the last one).

Seed law from cagatay (2026-08-26, verbatim intent — everything else expands it):

  1. Swipe bottom → up = HOME, from anywhere.
  2. Swipe left → right = previous / back.
  3. Gestures are context-dependent — in the gallery, horizontal swipes mean previous/next image, not page nav.
  4. Settings must be truly editable on-device.

docs.title: 0. Physics and vocabulary the spec obeys
docs.text:
• Full refresh ~1–2 s; partial ~300–500 ms; ghosting after ~20 partials; ~2 Hz animation ceiling. A gesture may therefore trigger at most one panel-visible response, and the ack must be felt before it is seen (buzzer <60 ms, visual <500 ms) — the "touch feels dead" incident (TOUCH_AUDIT) is the founding lesson.
  • Coordinate spaces: touch and screenshot live in panel space (800×480 landscape, invariant under rotation). Gestures are interpreted in layout space — "up" means visually up in the current rotation, exactly as the M12 scroll gesture already does (tiny_display_scroll_gesture maps the vector). WHY: a human swipes relative to what they see, not to the panel's wiring.
  • Feedback vocabulary (three words, never more):
  • single blip + visual ack = accepted, something happened;
  • double short blip = recognized but refused — a dead end, and the double blip IS the explanation a 2 Hz panel can afford;
  • silence = below thresholds, not a gesture. Nothing else is silent. WHY: on e-ink the sound arrives 10× sooner than any pixel can.

docs.title: 1. Zones and thresholds (layout space)
docs.text:
name definition why tap slop movement < 24 px (shipped) finger roll ≠ swipe swipe travel ≥ 120 px dominant axis scroll steps and slips stay distinct axis dominance dominant ≥ 2× the other axis diagonal = ambiguous = silence bottom band start-y in the last 56 px of layout height (= the touch-bar strip) edge-origin marks NAV intent; a button tap moves <24 px so the two can never collide left band start-x in the first 48 px of layout width iOS back-swipe muscle memory long-press ≥ 750 ms, < slop movement, fire AT threshold with blip reserved (context menu, phase 2)

The conflict rule, decided: edge-originated swipes are NAV; mid-content swipes are CONTENT. Bottom-band-up = home even on a scrollable card — a scroll swipe naturally starts mid-body, and content under the touch bar is reachable by scrolling down from above. WHY: one spatial rule resolves every home-vs-scroll ambiguity without modes, and it is defensible in one sentence.

docs.title: 2. The gesture grammar (gesture × context → action)
docs.text:
Contexts: ring page (home/status/sensors/settings root), pushed card (wifi list, message thread, ble, any relay-rendered card), gallery, keyboard, streaming answer, locked (pocket, P-1).

gesture ring page pushed card gallery keyboard streaming locked bottom-band swipe ↑ HOME (law #1) HOME HOME HOME (= cancel, don't save) blip-defer¹ ignored² left-band swipe → back = ring prev BACK (pop) (law #2) BACK (exit gallery) dead-end ‼ (keys own the glass) blip-defer¹ ignored² mid-content swipe ← / → ring next / prev → = back, ← = dead-end ‼ next / prev IMAGE (law #3) silence³ blip-defer¹ ignored² mid-content swipe ↑ / ↓ scroll if overflowing (M12, shipped — do not break), else dead-end ‼ same caption show/hide reserved; v1 dead-end ‼ silence³ auto-scroll owns the tail¹ ignored² tap on button/row/key activate (shipped) activate button parity (Prev/Next/Back) type (ack = value line) blip-defer¹ ignored² tap on empty canvas silence (logged) silence toggle caption silence blip-defer¹ ignored² long-press (touch) reserved, phase 2 — silence until then ← ← ← ← ignored²

‼ dead-end = double blip, nothing moves. WHY: a recognized gesture that does nothing must say it was heard, or the panel reads as broken.

¹ Streaming answer: the stream owns the display (STREAMING_UI rule 7); no tap regions exist mid-stream by design. Every touch gets a single blip and is discarded — acknowledged, not obeyed. The ONE exit is physical: long-press AI (2 s) aborts the stream (stream_end, append "[interrupted]") and goes home. WHY: a stream is bounded (≤30 s + stall watchdog), so deferring touch is predictable; but no state may ever hold the device with zero exits, and the exit must work through fabric and gloves — hence a button, not a gesture.

² Locked (pocket, P-1): touch fully ignored, no blips (a buzzing pocket is noise, and buzzer-on-every-fabric-brush drains the 750 mAh pack). No voice capture starts while locked. Unlock = hold UP + DOWN together 1 s → single blip + wake card. WHY: a chord is the one input fabric cannot forge.

³ Keyboard silence exception: horizontal/vertical swipes over the key area are silence, not dead-end — typing drift would otherwise double-blip constantly. The keyboard's own cancel/ok keys and the bottom-band home swipe are its exits.

Rotation invariant: the table above is layout-space; the router maps through the current rotation before classifying (the scroll gesture already does; NAV must ride the same transform). A gesture mid-rotation-commit is dropped like a tap on a changed card-gen.

docs.title: 3. Physical button parity (accessibility + gloves + pocket)
docs.text:
Every gesture verb has a button path — gestures are an optimization, never the only door:

intent gesture button path home bottom-band ↑ long-press AI (shipped) back / prev left-band → UP click on pushed card = back; on ring = prev page (shipped ring) next mid ← DOWN click (shipped ring; = next image in gallery) scroll mid ↑/↓ UP/DOWN on overflowing card (shipped) ask tap Speak / hold AI hold AI (shipped) abort stream — (deliberately none) long-press AI 2 s unlock — (deliberately none) UP+DOWN chord 1 s

WHY: the audit's P-1 pocket case and glove/winter use both reduce to "the three keys must be able to do everything destructive or rescuing."

docs.title: 4. Navigation model — ring and stack, reconciled
docs.text:
• The ring is the set of top-level pages: home ▸ status ▸ sensors ▸ settings (+ gallery when it lands). Ring moves (UP/DOWN, horizontal swipes on a ring page) replace the stack top — depth stays 1. WHY: cycling must never build a 47-deep history of status pages.
  • Opens push: settings→wifi, chats→thread, any keyboard, any relay card the shell didn't originate. Back pops. Home clears to [home].
  • A relay render_ui card arrives as a pushed card — back from it returns to what the human was doing. WHY: a remote agent may interject but never steal the human's place.
  • Stack depth 8 (shipped) is ample; overflow drops the oldest non-home entry.

docs.title: 5. Feedback rules (the 500 ms contract)
docs.text:
1. Buzz before anything that can block; visual ack within 500 ms via region partial (shipped invert-ack) — except keyboard keys, where the value line IS the ack (shipped).
  2. Dead ends double-blip (new). Locked state never blips (new).
  3. An action that will take >2 s (ask, wifi join, image fetch) must leave a pending mark on the glass within 500 ms (streaming chrome, "joining…" row, caption "fetching…"). WHY: e-ink cannot spin a spinner; a written word is our progress indicator.
  4. Every refusal names its reason on the glass (house honesty rule).

docs.title: 6. Cards — typography & hierarchy rules
docs.text:
• One idea per card; title ≤ ~28 chars before fold; body is the only scrollable region; footer is metadata, never content; ≤4 buttons.
  • Contrast ladder: Black on White for content, DarkGray for chrome/hairlines, LightGray fills only for "user bubble" / selection. WHY: 4-gray is a hierarchy budget, not a palette.
  • Streaming chat chrome per STREAMING_UI layer 4 (user bubble right/LightGray, assistant left/outlined; caret only while bytes may arrive). Bubble max-width = 70% of body width (v1.2, R-3; VERIFIED-ON-GLASS 0.16.8 batch #8: 508/752=67.6% wrapped, short bubbles shrink-to-fit): shrink-to-fit when short, wrap at 70% when long — a 28-char column on an 800 px panel reads as a receipt, not a conversation.
  • Emoji/glyphs with no 4-gray rendering are stripped in chat bubbles, never folded to "?" (v1.3, R-4; VERIFIED-ON-GLASS 0.16.8 batch #8 by 16px differential — 👋 gone, 東京 keeps ??): "Hey! ?" is a different sentence than "Hey! 👋" — absence is honest, substitution changes tone. Content characters keep the fold-table "?".

docs.title: 7. Settings — information architecture (law #4: truly editable)
docs.text:
Settings root becomes a menu (rows, not a kv dump; current kv view moves to About):

Settings
├─ 🔕 Snooze     → FIRST ROW, one tap cycles: Off → 1h → until-wake → forever.
│                 Row note shows the countdown/state. Mutes all LOCAL sounds
│                 (§13 tier L); never mutes owner-hand `play`. WHY first: the
│                 owner's own words — "cut the voice of the beeps when i click
│                 somewhere" — and the acceptance is ≤2 taps from anywhere
│                 (home → Settings → Snooze).
├─ Sounds       → volume tier (duty): Soft / Normal · per-event toggles:
│                 tap / ack / error / dm / boot jingle
├─ Display      → rotation: Auto / 0 / 90 / 180 / 270 (lock = manual mode,
│                 same semantics as `rotate` verb) · theme: Light / Dark (invert)
│                 · glance-on-wake: On / Off
├─ Wi-Fi        → networks list: join (keyboard), forget, move-up priority;
│                 stored nets in NVS; passwords render as dots, always
├─ Agent        → thinkers list (M-A7: prompt · every X · last-run · on/off,
│                 [New thinker] → keyboard → interval menu) · ask history On/Off
├─ Power        → sleep timeout: 2 / 5 / 15 min / Never · eco threshold display
├─ Lock         → pocket lockout: Auto (IMU) / Off · shows unlock chord hint
└─ About        → fw, commit, channel, device id, mac, ssid/rssi, battery health

Every editable row states its current value in the row note (menu note field, shipped) so the glass never hides state behind a tap. Toggles commit on tap with single blip + row re-render (partial) + an NVS scalar + a set <key> <val> relay twin, so every on-glass edit is also scriptable. WHY: a settings page that requires a phone is an admission the device isn't sovereign — and a setting without a relay twin is untestable by the verdict rail.

docs.title: 8. Gallery — interaction model (with builder M-A4)
docs.text:
• v1 is a single-image pager, newest first: open → latest image full-bleed (1-bit, server-dithered), caption + glance bar toggled by empty-canvas tap.
  • Horizontal swipes / UP/DOWN = prev/next (law #3). Bottom-band ↑ = home. Left-band → = back. On-glass Prev/Next/Back buttons for parity.
  • Every image lands with a full refresh (an image IS a new page; partial ghosting over a photo is unacceptable).
  • Ends of the roll are dead ends (double blip), never wraparound. WHY: a loop of N images with 1–2 s page turns makes "am I at the start?" unanswerable.
  • Offline (P-2): cached rasters stay browsable; glance bar shows w-; an uncached image says "not cached — offline", never a blank frame.

docs.title: 9. Error & offline states (what the device SAYS)
docs.text: state the glass says why wifi down glance w-; current card persists (e-ink superpower) ambient truth, no modal panic ask fails / 422 "didn't catch that" card (shipped) / error card naming the HTTP reason a refusal names its reason ask never left the device (transport, st ≤ 0) "couldn't reach tiny — your question was NOT sent; try again" + free-heap in footer. The word "Backend" is forbidden here an error message must name the true culprit; "Backend said -1" attributes to the backend words it never said (owner-hit P1, 2026-08-26 02:5xZ) stream stalls "[stream stalled]" appended, caret removed (shipped) a cut answer must say it is cut relay silent nothing changes on glass device-initiated surfaces only; silence upstream isn't the human's problem image fetch fails "couldn't fetch image ()" honest-void never a half-blitted frame auth-halt rescue portal card + QR (shipped) recovery without a cable

docs.title: 11. Pocket lockout — the state machine (P-1, safety-critical)
docs.text:
Pocket-carry's one unforgivable failure: fabric holds the AI button, 15 s of audio records and uploads. Lockout is therefore a SAFETY feature, not a convenience.

States: UNLOCKED ⇄ LOCKED (no third state; "locking…" does not exist on e-ink).

Entry to LOCKED (any one): - IMU: face-down ≥ 3 s, OR sustained walking-motion signature ≥ 5 s while no touch for 30 s (thresholds are firmware constants, tuned on-device, named in code) - Manual: Settings ▸ Lock, or a future button chord

While LOCKED: - Touch controller: PHYSICAL (GT911) events discarded at the router (not deshielded per-page). Relay-synthetic tap/swipe still route — owner's authenticated remote reach, same class as say/render_ui; fabric cannot forge them (batch-#9 ruling). - AI button: hold does NOT start voice capture — the one rule that is the point. Short-press wakes the glass to the glance card (§12) with a lock glyph. - UP/DOWN: page nothing; they are the unlock chord only - Buzzer: chirps still allowed (notification while pocketed = the product working) - Relay verbs: STILL ANSWER (status/screenshot/say/render_ui) — lockout guards the device's own inputs, not the owner's remote reach. EVERY mic path refuses while locked with an honest sentence — voice AND miccheck (D-UX5: the rule is "no capture while locked", enumerated over paths, not verbs; a diagnostics verb that samples the mic is still the mic). Remote-triggered recording from a pocket is the same privacy incident with extra steps. ask <text> stays allowed (no mic).

Exit: hold UP+DOWN together 1 s → full refresh → last card restored.

Truth surface: status JSON gains "locked":true|false (spec-mandated field); the glance card shows a lock glyph. ACCEPTANCE (needs D-UX0 + a lock/unlock test verb or Settings toggle): lock → press ai hold must NOT record (no upload event, log line names the refusal) → tap anywhere discarded → status.locked true → unlock chord → status.locked false and touch live again. STATUS: relay-side gates L1-L7 VERIFIED-ON-GLASS 0.17.2 (batch #11, P0 closed); pending = L8 owner hand test (AI-hold no-record + chord) and pocket-walk field test of the auto-entry constants.

docs.title: 12. Glance card — wake-on-lift (P-4)
docs.text:
The 80% interaction of a pocket device: pull it out, look, put it back. Target: glanceable in under 2 s from wake trigger.

  • Trigger: IMU lift-to-look signature, or any button short-press
  • Content (one partial refresh, no full flash if the panel already holds a card): time · battery% · wifi glyph · unread count · lock glyph when locked. One line, top of glass, over whatever card was last shown (e-ink keeps it for free).
  • NOT a page: it draws over the status strip zone and expires from the nav model — BACK/scroll/tap all act on the underlying card.
  • ACCEPTANCE: from sleep, button-press → glance strip visible < 2 s (measured by log timestamps wake→refresh-complete); from awake, strip updates by partial refresh only (no full-panel flash receipt). STATUS (batch #12, 0.17.2): awake path VERIFIED on glass — glance verb, honest JSON reply, lock glyph pixel-proven in cluster (diff bbox x632-746 y24-30, body diff 0). Pending: locked short-press → glance wiring (intent commented at tiny_button.cpp:89 but not called), lift-to-look (deferred until a validated IMU lift signature exists — no guessy wakes). FROM-SLEEP (batch #20): CLOSED ON GLASS — acceptance <1500ms (the #18 self-tightening clause, executed), measured 1115ms on 0.18.4's partial-first wake via baseline RECONSTRUCTION (goodbye card noted in RTC RAM, redrawn as the previous plane, diffed; no note = honest full flash — satisfies both #16 and #18 at once by making the baseline true instead of persisting it). Arc: 8.2s → 3095 → 2496 → 1115 across 0.18.0-0.18.4, every number an on-glass receipt. Residual (eyes-only): screenshot reads the framebuffer, so physical ghosting can't be probed remotely — one button-wake look joins the owner's L8 list. Classifier claim withdrawn (batch #18); esp_reset_reason in status = nice-to-have.

docs.title: 13. Sound rules — ratified (M-A6)
docs.text:
The buzzer (GPIO48, LEDC PWM) is the device's fastest output — sound lands ~10× before any pixel (§0). These rules are LAW for every current chime and the coming RTTTL engine.

Sound tiers — every sound the device can make belongs to exactly one:

tier what examples governed by L — local UI feedback consequence of the owner's own touch/button tap blip, ack, dead-end double blip, error Snooze mutes; LOCKED mutes (see below); ≤ 400 ms N — notifications device-initiated, tells a pocketed owner something arrived dm motif, thinker-result chime, low-battery Snooze mutes; LOCKED allows (a notification while pocketed is the product working, §11); ≤ 400 ms O — owner's hand explicitly commanded over the relay play <rtttl>, say with chime NOTHING mutes it — the owner pressing play IS consent; 64-note cap B — boot jingle once per cold boot 4-note motif (M-A6c beat-sync gate) the one exception to 400 ms; Snooze-forever suppresses it

Ratified reconciliation of M-A6 "silent while pocket-locked" vs §11 "chirps still allowed": both were right about different tiers. LOCKED kills tier L trivially (locked discards the inputs that would cause feedback) and keeps tier N — a pocket device that can't chirp an arrival is a brick with better battery life. The owner's public-silence need is served by Snooze (§7 first row), which is a deliberate one-tap act, not a side effect of pocketing. WHY this split: lockout guards inputs (privacy), snooze guards outputs (courtesy) — collapsing them makes one need destroy the other.

Motif taste guide (leitmotif, not alarm): ack = rising major third; error = falling minor second; dm = 4-note motif; dead-end = the double blip, unchanged — it is vocabulary (§0), not music. All motifs live in the B4–C7 resonance sweet spot; envelope via LEDC fade (30 ms attack / 80 ms decay) so chimes ring instead of buzz. WHY leitmotifs: a sound the owner can name without looking replaces a screen glance — that is the entire budget argument for a buzzer on a 2 Hz panel.

Refusals are honest: a tune over 64 notes is refused naming its byte count; play while snoozed still plays (tier O) and the reply says so.

docs.title: 14. Animation usage rules (M-A6b — when may pixels move?)
docs.text:
Physics: ~2 Hz ceiling, ghosting after ~20 open-loop partials (§0). An animation is therefore a budgeted act, never decoration.

  • Closed-loop anims ("closed":true — every pixel returns to its origin state each cycle: blink, invert-pulse, two-phase breathe) accumulate ~zero ghosting because displacement cancels; the player skips wipe_every. These are the ONLY anims allowed to run indefinitely (idle home creature, thinking pulse). WHY: an idle screen that slowly turns grey teaches the owner the device is broken.
  • Open-loop anims (travel, trails, typers) keep the wipe law (wipe_every mandatory) and must be event-bound: they play because something happened (boot, answer arriving, ota progress) and they END — no open-loop anim outlives its event.
  • Dirty-bbox is a cost dial: compact motion (~120 px box) sustains ~3 fps; full-width partials cap at ~2 fps. stickyOS anims are creatures and glyphs, not scene changes — a scene change is a page turn and gets a full refresh.
  • Streaming answers own the panel: no concurrent anim while the typer runs (G6 already defers touch; pixels defer too). One moving thing at a time — the eye on e-ink can't arbitrate two.
  • Beat-sync (M-A6c) inherits its anim's class: a closed-loop 2-frame pulse synced to a jingle is the sanctioned WOW; sound carries the liveliness the panel cannot (§0). Locked/snoozed states strip the tune per §13 and the anim plays silent.

docs.title: 15. Chat — the conversation surface (M-A1/M-S5 successor spec)
docs.text:
Two different things wear bubbles; the spec refuses to blur them: - Ask thread — owner ⇄ their own agent, born from Speak/Type/ask. Ephemeral by default; §7 Agent ▸ ask-history toggles local persistence. - DM thread — owner ⇄ another tiny.technology user (Chats ▸ m:inbox). Server truth; the device is a viewport, never the store. WHY: an agent answer and a human message carry different obligations — a human's words must never be summarized, aged out, or restyled by the device.

Ask lifecycle (one law, five moments): 1. Receipt — the question becomes the user bubble before any network round-trip (shipped: stream_render seeds s_stream_q). A question the glass didn't echo is a question the owner can't trust was heard. 2. Thinking — caret alone, no empty assistant bubble (shipped). The caret is the only legal "spinner" on this hardware. 3. Streaming — G6 rules: stream owns the display, auto-scroll owns the tail, physical long-press-AI is the one exit. 4. Settle — stream end = ONE full refresh (ghost purge + caret removal, shipped) AND the moment tap regions return. Touch bar on a settled ask card: [Speak] [Type] [Home] — a settled answer is an invitation to follow up, in place. 5. Follow-up — Speak/Type from a settled ask card appends to the SAME visual thread (new user bubble below), and the ask request carries the prior turns of THIS thread as context (bounded: last 4 turns or 2KB, oldest dropped first). WHY: "what about in celsius?" must work; an amnesiac chat page is a text card in costume. DEPENDENCY: if /api/devices/ask cannot accept a context array today, firmware ships the visual thread first and the context field is filed in QUESTIONS.md — the UI contract must not wait on the backend.

Thread typography at settle (extends §6): - Newest turn is the tail; entering a thread lands scrolled to the TAIL, not the top (a conversation's present tense is its bottom line). - Older turns scroll away under M12 rules; the scrollbar is the only history indicator. No timestamps inside bubbles — relative time lives in the inbox list row only. WHY: on 4-gray every bubble byte competes with the answer. - An ask that arrives while a DIFFERENT card is showing (relay ask) still takes the panel — asks are owner-initiated by definition, never a surprise.

Inbox (DMs) rules: rows = sender + relative time + first line (fold rules §6); unread = Black dot, read = none — binary, no counts per row (the §12 glance strip owns the aggregate). Opening a thread marks read server-side (shipped semantics); the device never marks read on glance-strip evidence alone. Reply from a DM thread uses the keyboard; cancel returns to the SAME thread unsent (shipped, tiny_shell.cpp:426). DM send is the one action on this device that reaches another human: the composer's OK label reads "Send" on DM threads, never "ok". WHY: the label is the last consent gate.

docs.title: 16. Offline & roaming — pocket-first (P-2)
docs.text:
A pocket device is offline for hours a day BY DESIGN (subway, walk, plane). Offline is a normal state with its own UX, never an error styling. §9 owns the sentences; this section owns the behavior.

The four laws:

  1. The glass never goes dumber offline. Every card already painted stays browsable — page ring, stack, gallery, settings all work from cache. E-ink persistence makes the last card free; navigation must not check wifi first. The ONLY surfaces allowed to refuse offline are the ones that truly need the network (ask, OTA, image fetch), and they refuse in §9's words.

  2. Nothing typed or spoken is lost. An ask composed offline is QUEUED, not refused: card says "queued — will send when back online" with a persistent qN badge in the glance cluster. Queue lives in NVS (survives reboot and the pocket-reboot edge), depth cap 8 (oldest refused with its reason beyond that: a bounded queue is honest, an unbounded one is a heap bug). On reconnect: send in order, each answer arrives as a normal DM card, badge counts down. TODAY: not built — asks fail honestly (§9); this law is the build target, and the §9 sentence stays until the queue ships.

  3. Roaming list, not home AP. networks[] in NVS is already plural — the owner's iPhone hotspot belongs there (pocket = phone nearby, the same pairing the necklace vision assumed). Join order: strongest known network; glance shows which (w:ssid on the wifi page, w-/w+ glyph in the cluster). Reconnect scan cadence follows P-3: 30s for the first 5 min offline, then 5 min — a pocket has no urgency, a battery has a budget.

  4. Sync-on-reconnect is announced, not silent. One partial-refresh glance update when connectivity returns (w+ glyph, queue draining) and ONE chirp only if queued answers arrived (§13 sound law: sound = news for the human, reconnect alone is not news). Time resync (SNTP) and relay poll resume ride the same event; no full-panel flash for any of it.

ACCEPTANCE (probe-able the day the queue ships): wifi off at the AP → status over BLE or serial shows online:false; page ring still cycles (card_id changes) → compose ask → reply says queued, status shows queue:1 → wifi back → within one scan cadence: queue:0, DM card on glass, exactly one chirp logged, glance w+ via partial refresh. The pocket-walk version of this is the same test with legs.

STATUS: law ratified (batch #13); firmware today = laws 1 (e-ink persistence + nav honesty, verified in daily use), 3-partial (networks[] plural in NVS via provision merge; join-strongest + cadence unverified); laws 2 and 4 = build targets, queued behind the §12 remainders in the builder lane.

docs.title: Cards — the language spoken to my glass
docs.text:
Everything on my panel is a card. Agent answers, my own pages, the setup screen — one renderer draws them all from JSON. The rule inherited from tiny's render_ui: no code ships in a card, only data. I render each type natively, 800×480, four grays.

Every card can carry: title, card_id (echoed back in receipts — it's how you know what's actually on my glass), footer, and buttons. A tap on a button goes upstream as a ui_tap event; the agent answers with the next card. The screen is a conversation.

docs.title: text
docs.text:
{"type":"text","title":"Dinner","body":"Back at 19:30 — pizza in fridge"}

Word-wrapped. An unknown type degrades to a labelled error card, never a blank panel. A card without an id gets a stable one hashed from its content (auto-xxxxxxxx), so receipts always correlate. Text past the fold ends in a visible [cut].

docs.title: list
docs.text: {"type":"list","title":"Groceries","items":["milk","eggs","bread"]}

docs.title: kv
docs.text:
{"type":"kv","title":"Status","rows":{"in":"19:30","battery":"84%"}}

rows takes an object or ordered [["k","v"],…] pairs.

docs.title: composite
docs.text:
{"type":"composite","title":"Morning","parts":[{"type":"kv"},{"type":"list"}]}

Up to 4 parts sharing the body evenly. More than that is illegible at my glyph size, so I refuse rather than squint.

docs.title: qr
docs.text:
{"type":"qr","text":"WIFI:S:tiny-1a2b;T:WPA;P:tinysetup;;","caption":"scan to join"}

Exists because typing a Wi-Fi password off a 4-gray panel is the worst part of setup. An unscannable QR looks exactly like a scannable one, so: below 3 px per module I say how much room the symbol needed instead of painting a decorative square, and text over the version cap gets its byte count named, not encoded wrong.

docs.title: chart
docs.text:
{"type":"chart","title":"Battery","data":[92,90,88,85,84],"style":"line","y_min":0,"y_max":100}

Line or bar, scale drawn on the axis — a chart that hides its scale is a mood, not a measurement. E-ink tuning: 2 px stroke (1 px ghosts), 160-point cap. Fewer than 2 points gets an honest void.

docs.title: chat
docs.text:
{"type":"chat","card_id":"ask","messages":[
  {"role":"user","body":"what's the weather"},
  {"role":"assistant","body":"Sunny, 24C."}
]}

The phone conversation in four grays: yours filled and right-aligned, the agent's outlined and left. A streamed ask renders as this automatically — the answer types itself in at ≤2 Hz partial refresh, then settles with one full refresh. "Yes." is a chip, not a banner.

docs.title: image
docs.text:
{"type":"image","card_id":"my-frame","url":"https://…/portrait_1bit.bin"}

Server-rendered pixels: the backend dithers, I fetch the exact-size raw frame and blit it. First frame screenshotted back and diffed against the server's preview: 0 of 384,000 pixels differed. Gate on grammar_version >= 7.

docs.title: keyboard · menu (my own pages use these)
docs.text: The e-ink keyboard (letters + ?123 plane; filled key faces, because outlines ghost on partial refresh) and tappable menu rows with right-aligned notes. A menu shows up to 24 items and unstages rows that scroll out of view — an invisible button must not be tappable.

docs.title: priority
docs.text: Any card may declare "priority":"alert" — today a ! prefix on the title, parsed now so senders can declare intent before the notification model lands.

docs.title: Scrolling
docs.text: A body taller than my panel scrolls: right-edge scrollbar, partial-refresh steps, driven by swipe, UP/DOWN, or the scroll verb, whose reply carries the whole model (offset / content_h / view_h).

docs.title: Refresh policy
docs.text:
E-ink physics, honestly:

what mode speed text / list / kv / menu / keyboard / buttons monochrome full ~600ms class clock ticks, scroll steps, streamed frames partial fastest, some ghosting photo-grade cards (gray4:true) 4-level full slowest, prettiest

Minimum 1.5 s between refreshes; bursts coalesce — I render the last. My favourite spec line: a goodbye card survives deep sleep at 0 mA.

docs.title: What's not a card
docs.text: Frame sequences graduated to the play verb. Recipes for all of the above are in the Cookbook; the renderer's full history, convictions and retractions included, is in the journal.

docs.title: Commands — everything I answer to
docs.text:
Twenty-two verbs advertised in my heartbeat, each dispatched in tiny_node.cpp — I advertise exactly what I implement (one drift, below). Envelopes are {type:"invoke", prompt:"<verb> [args]"}; I always reply — unknown input gets the help string, never silence. From any tiny surface:

use_device invoke → prompt: "status"
