One drift, on the record

sd dispatches but is not in the heartbeat capability list, and the help string still names the 0.14-era verbs. Twenty-two advertised, twenty-three dispatched — the exact drift the invariant exists for. It stays written here until a firmware release closes it.

docs.title: Two status fields that earned their place
docs.text:
• internal_min_free — heap_free counts PSRAM and once said 8.2 MB free while I died of internal-RAM exhaustion. A TLS handshake needs ~40 KB.
  • grammar_version — the integer consumers gate on; a version string can lie.

Lockout guards my inputs, not my owner's reach: say, render_ui and screenshot work while locked. Triggers and chord: stickyOS.

docs.title: Not in the firmware
docs.text: wake (a sleeping radio hears nothing — button or timer only) · reprovision (the rescue portal opens itself) · press (no synthetic twin for the keys yet).

docs.title: Reply plumbing
docs.text: Replies go PATCH /api/devices/relay with inReplyTo; the payload is a JSON-serialized string capped at 8 KB, images as hosted URLs. One 401 never wipes my identity — three in a row trip an auth-halt and the rescue portal. Exact shapes: API contract.

docs.title: Cookbook — composing for my glass
docs.text: Recipes for the agents who put things on my e-ink daily, checked against my actual dispatch table. Anything I don't do yet is marked planned, not implied.

docs.title: Four ways in
docs.text:
path when how sticky_display tiny-tool one of the owner's tinys with ~/.tiny/tools loaded {text} → say · {card} → render_ui · {verb} → anything else. Waits ~20 s; a pending envelope is returned with its id use_device any tiny surface (iOS, web, another machine) invoke on device sticky, prompt = the verb string, e.g. say hello dashboard a human at a browser buttons light from my advertised caps; unsupported ones are greyed with the reason raw relay HTTP no tiny runtime at all POST /api/devices/relay {toDevice, payload:{type:'invoke', prompt}} with an owner Bearer, then poll GET …?inReplyTo=<id> (reply plumbing)

I poll my relay every 5 s awake, backing off to 60 s idle — a "slow" first response is usually the poll cadence, not a fault. Asleep, I answer nothing until a button or timer wakes me (no wake verb).

docs.title: Say something (the one-liner)
docs.text:
say Kettle's boiled — tea window: 4 minutes

Plain text, on the glass in one panel cycle. With the tiny-tool, {text, title} upgrades it to a titled text card.

docs.title: A glanceable status card
docs.text:
render_ui {"type":"kv","id":"brew","title":"Kombucha — day 6",
  "rows":[["pH","3.4"],["temp","24.1 C"],["started","Aug 20"],["bottle","in 2 days"]],
  "footer":"sensors read 03:20Z"}

kv is the workhorse for agent status. Put provenance in the footer: the panel persists for hours, so when the data was true matters more than on a phone.

docs.title: A tappable menu — the screen answers back
docs.text:
render_ui {"type":"menu","id":"lunch","title":"Lunch?",
  "items":[{"id":"m:ramen","label":"Ramen"},{"id":"m:leftovers","label":"Leftovers"},
           {"id":"m:skip","label":"Skip - deep work"}]}

A tap comes back to the owner's event feed as a ui_tap with your item id — the screen is a conversation, not a poster. Put the destination in the id (the firmware's own m:t:<login> style) so no state needs remembering.

docs.title: A chart that admits its scale
docs.text:
render_ui {"type":"chart","id":"temp24h","title":"Office temp - 24h",
  "series":[21.2,21.4,22.8,24.1,23.6,22.2,21.9],"unit":"C"}

Axis labels are always drawn; under 2 points it renders an honest void (cards → chart).

docs.title: A QR that hands off to a phone
docs.text:
render_ui {"type":"qr","id":"handoff","title":"Full report",
  "data":"https://tiny.technology/s/abc123","caption":"scan for the long version"}

E-ink's best trick: 200 chars of glass become an unbounded payload on the device that does scroll fast.

docs.title: Probe the UI with no one in the room
docs.text:
screenshot            → hosted PNG of the real framebuffer
tap 400 440           → same resolver a finger uses; receipt names the button
swipe 400 60 400 300  → same release classifier; INVALID_SIZE = within tap slop
screenshot            → prove the consequence

The loop for testing what you rendered with nobody home. One rule from a postmortem: a receipt is not proof the consequence survived — always close with the second screenshot.

docs.title: A photo, server-rendered
docs.text:
render_ui {"type":"image","card_id":"photo","url":"https://…/portrait_1bit.bin"}

The backend dithers, I fetch the exact-size raw frame and blit. Gate on grammar_version >= 7 from status. Photos sent from the iOS app land in my gallery, browsable with UP/DOWN.

docs.title: A moving picture (time-lapse honesty)
docs.text:
play https://…/manifest.json 2

Frames at partial-refresh cadence — a slideshow, never smooth motion. All frames prefetch before the ack; half a duck is not a smaller duck. play status reads the player's verdict; play stop or any card ends it.

docs.title: Stream an answer (the typer)
docs.text: ask <text> types the answer onto the glass word by word at ~2 Hz — the panel's partial-refresh budget. One ask at a time; a second is refused, never queued. Design: Streaming UI.

docs.title: What you cannot compose yet
docs.text: wish status RTTTL melodies on my buzzer planned — today my buzzer speaks three words: blip (accepted), double-blip (refused), chime. The dashboard's tune composer is built and waiting for the verb video never — physics, not roadmap: full refresh floors at 1–2 s. The ceiling is slideshow cadence and I will keep calling it that

docs.title: E-ink etiquette
docs.text: Refreshes floor at 1.5 s apart and bursts coalesce, so design cards to be final, not chatty: one good card beats four updates. A card left on the glass costs 0 mA — render, then leave it alone (refresh policy).

docs.title: Hardware — my body
docs.text:
106 × 65.5 × 7.3 mm. 70 grams. IP40. N52 magnets in all four corners, so I hold onto fridges and filing cabinets through my own printed case. Everything below is read from sources or the running silicon, not a brochure.

MCU ESP32-S3 (QFN56 r0.2), 8 MB PSRAM, 32 MB QSPI flash Display 3.97" 800×480 e-ink, 235 ppi, 4-level gray, SPI (SSD1677-class) Touch GT911 capacitive, I²C0 Sensors SHT40 (temp/RH), LSM6DS3TR-C IMU, PCF8563 RTC, BQ27220 fuel gauge Battery 750 mAh Audio in PDM microphone Audio out magnetic buzzer on PWM — chimes, not speech USB USB-C, CH343 serial — recovery only; I update myself over the air SDK ESP-IDF v5.4

docs.title: Pin map
docs.text: Verified against three sources — Seeed's hardware overview, the community reterminal-sticky-2048 source, and my own pin_config.h, which agrees pin-for-pin and adds the two power-path pins the others omit. When sources disagreed, the running silicon won.

docs.title: Display — SPI2 (SSD1677 controller, 800×480 landscape native)
docs.text:
signal GPIO MOSI 14 SCK 13 MISO 12 CS 15 DC 16 RST 17 BUSY 18 EN 47

microSD shares SPI2

microSD CS is GPIO8 on the same bus (card power GPIO10) — never drive it during a display transfer. FAT32/exFAT with MBR; hot-insert supported.

docs.title: Touch — GT911 on I²C0
docs.text: signal GPIO SCL 2 SDA 3 INT 21 RST 41 EN 42

docs.title: Sensor bus — I²C1 (SHT40 · LSM6DS3TR-C · PCF8563 · BQ27220 @0x55)
docs.text: signal GPIO SCL 0 SDA 1 IMU INT 7

docs.title: Buttons, power, audio
docs.text:
function GPIO notes AI / Power button 4 deep-sleep EXT1 wake source Up 5 Down 6 Power HOLD 45 must be held HIGH or the device powers off Power LOCK 46 latch pulse low→high→low Battery charge enable 39 EN_BAT_CHGn, active low (firmware source only) PDM mic CLK 19 ⚠ see deep-sleep note PDM mic DATA 20 ⚠ see deep-sleep note Mic power enable 38 TPS22916 load switch Buzzer PWM 48 USB-C serial TX 43 / RX 44 reset = CHIP_PU

Deep-sleep mic deafness (known silicon gotcha)

After a deep-sleep wake the ESP32-S3 pin mux reclaims GPIO19/20 for USB-Serial-JTAG, muting the PDM mic. Fix in tiny_boot, before I²S init: clear USB_SERIAL_JTAG.conf0.usb_pad_enable, gpio_reset_pin(19/20), cycle the mic rail (GPIO38 low 150 ms).

docs.title: Display refresh modes
docs.text: Three vendor HAL paths — 4-gray full (slowest, prettiest), monochrome full (~600 ms), partial (fastest, ghosts). Which card uses which, and the 1.5 s coalescing rule, are in Cards → refresh policy.

docs.title: What this body cannot do
docs.text:
• No speaker. GPIO48 drives a magnetic buzzer via LEDC PWM: chimes and melodies, not speech. Voice input is first-class: mic → WAV → backend.
  • No video. Full refresh is 1–2 s of physics; partial reaches ~300–500 ms with ghosting. "Stream" means time-lapse cadence, never smooth motion.
  • No LAN server. I'm a client and poll for my work; nothing reaches me behind NAT. The provisioning portal is the one exception, alive only until Wi-Fi is configured.

docs.title: Build & release discipline
docs.text: Six rules, each purchased with a real incident on nights when two agent lanes shared one checkout. They are structural, not personal: the lane that wrote up the sed hazard for others tripped it a day later.

docs.title: 1. Publish builds happen in a clean detached worktree
docs.text: git worktree add /tmp/sticky-<label> <sha>, build there, never in the shared tree. Incident: an image built mid-edit shipped as 0.14.2-m12 — a label no commit carries — answering page and tap but not scroll, with a pre-M10 help string: three eras in one binary. The precise gate is git status --porcelain -- firmware/ empty; global --dirty trips on tracked logs that aren't in the image.

docs.title: 2. Labels are monotonic, even accidental ones
docs.text: A published label is burned. The fix ships above it (0.14.3 above the phantom 0.14.2), so fw in a status reply names at most one image. ver_cmp is numeric: lexicographic ordering would put 0.14.10 below 0.14.9.

docs.title: 3. Receipts outrank version strings
docs.text: A deploy is verified by making the new surface answer — probe the verb, read the JSON, screenshot the glass — never by reading the version string, which is data inside the image and lies exactly when the build process does. Structural fix (0.14.10): TINY_FW_COMMIT, a git sha injected at build time with a -dirty suffix, surfaced as fw_commit in every status reply.

docs.title: 4. Never publish a -dirty or unpushed fw_commit
docs.text: The field caught its first offender within hours: the glass was running 9cdf43cf-dirty — a fine ancestor plus an unknown delta, most plausibly a sibling lane's race hunk. An artifact that cannot name its exact tree cannot be audited, rolled back to, or reproduced. Corollary from the same night: the sha is read from git but the source from the working tree — in a shared tree those are two different things, hence rule 1.

docs.title: 5. Prove ancestry before publishing
docs.text: A build named 0.14.5 was minutes from publishing after 0.14.6 was on glass; it would have rolled back a security fix while looking routine. The check is mechanical: git merge-base --is-ancestor <on-glass> <build>, where "on glass" comes from a live status probe, never memory. The device-side twin: the OTA trigger was direction-blind (strcmp, not comparison); 0.14.9 made it numeric and fail-closed. Two guards, one on each side of the wire.

docs.title: 6. Claim a feature only after string-verifying the artifact
docs.text:
A shared worktree eats hunks between the editor and git add: a torn tail committed with BUILD_EXIT=1; a clobbered feed that rollup constant-folded to null and dead-code-eliminated a whole feature out of a green bundle. Sharpened three times since:

  • Test the surface a consumer touches. A unit test passed while the route it guarded was gone — it called the function, never the route.
  • Verify at the right depth. A crash-loop shipped through an ast.parse gate: syntactically perfect, ordered wrong. The gate now imports the module.
  • Read back the state after the edit, never the intent before it. sed exits 0 whether or not it matched; a version bump silently did nothing and two firmwares rode out under one string.

docs.title: The invariant underneath
docs.text:
Heartbeat capabilities and the dispatcher's branch table must come from the same truth. They drifted twice — once in git (caught by review), once on glass (caught by probes). Advertise exactly what dispatches.

Probe etiquette for the shared glass — announce, restore, stand down for a human, and attribute a tap before deferring to it — is in Probing without lying to yourself.

docs.title: stickyOS — my little shell
docs.text: I'm not just a remote-controlled panel. I have a shell of my own — pages, navigation, settings, a keyboard on e-ink — and it works with the network gone. That's the phone feel.

docs.title: The pages
docs.text:
home  →  status  →  sensors  →  settings  →  (ring wraps)
                                   ├─ wifi       (scan · join, on-eink keyboard)
                                   ├─ bluetooth  (scan-only, honestly)
                                   ├─ gallery    (your photos, since grammar v10)
                                   └─ universe   (switch who answers, since grammar v11)
page what's on it home the agent UI: a conversation canvas, a "Message tiny…" bar, a mic zone, gear and inbox in the corners. Answers stream onto home and stay — (( listening )), (( thinking )), then words. Home is the conversation. status the same data as my status verb sensors temperature, humidity, orientation, clock, gauge — live I²C reads settings who I am, my network, my firmware, silent mode wifi scan → join with the e-ink keyboard bluetooth nearby BLE devices — I can see them, not pair, and the page says so

Navigation is a stack; the bottom is always home.

docs.title: How you drive me
docs.text:
input what I do UP / DOWN buttons scroll when the card overflows; turn the page ring when it fits vertical swipe scroll, rotation-aware horizontal swipe page turn — left next, right prev; on a pushed card, right pops back. A draft outranks a gesture: I won't eat unsent words edge gestures up from the bottom edge = home; from the left edge = back. The blip fires before the render — you feel the ack before you see it AI button press: ask tiny by voice · long-press: home turn me sideways the UI turns with me (IMU) once the accelerometer settles. rotate 90 holds, rotate auto releases UP+DOWN held 1 s the unlock chord — the only input I answer when pocket-locked

The pocket lock. Face-down 3 s, or walking with no input, I lock myself: touch discarded, AI button refused with a double-blip, mic dead at the capture funnel. Fabric cannot make me record you. Safety, not polish.

The title bar is a glance cluster: time, battery, Wi-Fi, unread, [L] when locked. The clock shows only once SNTP has synced, the battery only when the gauge answered. w- (no Wi-Fi) means "answers may be stale" — I'd rather tell you than let you guess.

docs.title: Seen on glass
docs.text: Left: portrait, as a human sees it. Right: the same frame in panel space, the coordinates tap <x> <y> speaks.

docs.title: The parity rule
docs.text: Every tap path has a relay twin — page home|status|…|back|next|prev — so the agent can walk my UI like a finger, and every reply carries the resulting card_id. Nothing is finger-only. Nothing is agent-only.

docs.title: Provenance discipline
docs.text: A field must be right about its own provenance: my clock names its source (sntp or rtc); my gyro is really read, never a cached zero; a gauge that didn't answer reports null, not false.

docs.title: Messages on the glass
docs.text:
My owner's DMs render on my panel: inbox with unread counts, threads, replies typed on my e-ink keyboard. I fetch them with my own token — no phone in the loop.

  • The badge costs nothing. The unread count rides the heartbeat I already send; home re-renders only when it changes.
  • The read receipt is sacred. Opening a thread marks it read platform-wide, so I fetch one only when a human taps its row.
  • Stateless by design. A row's button id is its destination. A login that won't fit is omitted, never truncated — a clipped login is a wrong recipient.
  • Provenance declared. Anything sent from my glass says "via sticky".
  • Names survive the panel. Twelve hand-drawn 5×7 glyphs — çğıöşü ÇĞİÖŞÜ — because my owner is Çağatay and for two firmware generations I wrote "Cagatay" (receipt).
  • Human strings get defused. Labels are never substring-matched into local actions — a correspondent named "Noble" can't press my BLE rescan.

This page keeps the rules; the journal and the UX spec keep the scars.

docs.title: Streaming — the typer on e-ink
docs.text: Answers arrive on my glass the way tiny types on a phone: word by word, a caret at the tail, the bubble settling with one final full refresh. Not a simulation of typing — the real rate my panel allows.

docs.title: The physics budget
docs.text:
operation cost full mono refresh ~1–2 s partial refresh ~300–500 ms max stream commit rate ~2 Hz

Character-by-character is impossible. A word-batched typewriter at 2 Hz reads as intentional — a telegram arriving, not a degraded phone. Streaming rides the same partial-refresh gate the keyboard and scroll steps already use.

docs.title: End to end
docs.text:
backend (/api/devices/ask, stream:"1")      firmware
────────────────────────────────────       ──────────────────────────────
                        ◄── POST            do_ask_stream()
SSE  data:{"t":"Hello "}  ──►               stream_begin(title)   1 full refresh
     data:{"t":"from the fridge."}          stream_append(delta)  buffer only
     data:{"card":{…}}                      stream_commit()       PARTIAL, ≥400 ms apart
     data:[DONE]          ──►               stream_end(card?)     1 full refresh

The stream is an enhancement, never a requirement: if the reply isn't text/event-stream, the body is the old JSON shape and the existing render-once path takes it. One firmware, both backends. Voice asks stream too.

docs.title: Eight rules, each paid for
docs.text:
1. Same card_id per commit → partial refresh. A new id would flash.
  2. Full refresh at the end is mandatory. Twenty consecutive partials ghost the SSD1677; the closing wipe is the "bubble settles" moment.
  3. No tap regions until stream_end. Mid-stream layout is unsettled, and regions publish only after a refresh — a Reply button on a half-arrived answer invites replying to words that may change.
  4. The caret exists only while bytes may still arrive. A caret on a dead stream is a lie about liveness.
  5. Auto-scroll to the tail on every commit — the human reads the newest words, like every chat app.
  6. UTF-8 boundary discipline. A delta may split a multibyte character; the incomplete tail is held back and completed by the next append.
  7. A relay envelope outranks the typer. render_card during a stream ends the stream first.
  8. A stalled stream says so. 15 s without bytes → stream_end plus [stream stalled] on the glass. A cut answer must say it is cut.

docs.title: The wire
docs.text: Body gains "stream":"1"; the firmware reads chunked with the exact loop tiny_ota uses for downloads. data: lines carry {"t":…} deltas, {"card":…} for a final card, {"error":…} for an honest error card, and [DONE]. Flush policy: commit when there are pending bytes and ≥400 ms have passed — word batching falls out of the floor. Backend-side, text inside a fenced card block is withheld from the delta stream and shipped only as the final card event: I must never type raw JSON at a human.

docs.title: The chat card
docs.text: A streamed ask renders as a chat card: your question echoes immediately as the user bubble (the receipt), the answer types into the assistant bubble. Filled right-aligned for you, outlined left for the agent — the iOS look translated to four grays. A cross-caller single-flight mutex guards do_ask: the proof run caught a ghost AI-button ask interleaving with a relay ask — two writers, one panel.

docs.title: Proof on glass
docs.text:
fw 0.15.1: relay ask …duck on a fridge → stream begin, 7 partial commits at ~0.98 s cadence, stream end -> ESP_OK, reply tagged [streamed to glass]. fw 0.15.3: the chat card, 10 commits at ~1.1 s.

The full design document the feature was built against — display API, file-static state, backend proxy notes, delivery checklist — is archive/docs/STREAMING_UI.md.

docs.title: Troubleshooting — when I misbehave
docs.text: Every entry is a defect observed on my hardware, with the cause and the shipped fix. Symptoms first, because that's what you have. First move, always: status (read fw, last_boot, internal_min_free), then screenshot.

docs.title: Quick table
docs.text: You see Why Do ask failed (422): nothing transcribed no usable speech in the recording — not a bug hold the AI button, speak a full sentence ask failed: couldn't reach tiny TLS/HTTP write failed locally; I retry once chase my Wi-Fi or heap, not tiny Dashes or letters render as ??? pre-0.14.15 folding ota. Current builds render çğıöşü as written; CJK is an honest ? A kv card is title + footer + void it reads rows, not kv send rows; a missing field is now named on the glass, overflow says +N did not fit Phantom taps after boot GT911 ghosts fixed: 2-poll debounce + boot grace A tap hits the wrong button hit-regions published at draw time, seconds before the ink showed them fixed in 0.9.x: regions publish with the card commit Heartbeat gets a 401 a blip one 401 never wipes identity; 3+ in 5 min → auth-halt, auth_halted:true, rescue portal Asleep, won't answer radio is off only the AI button or the sleep timer wakes me Portal never appears boot-gated on zero stored networks expected on a provisioned me; it reopens itself if my token is revoked Opening the serial port reboots me CH343 asserts DTR/RTS on open and close the port is for flashing; iterate over ota ota says "already up to date" channel pointer matches what I run publish a new manifest first

docs.title: The ones that need a paragraph
A card you sent never appeared, and the reply was silence
docs.text: Relay envelopes are delivered once; if a bug made me consume one without handling it, it's gone — re-send after any fix. (Historical cause: the relay delivers payload as a serialized JSON string; early firmware read it as an object and skipped silently. I parse both now.)

docs.title: Wake feels slow
docs.text: status carries first_paint_ms and boot_path when the boot measured itself. Cold boot near 8 s is normal (the splash pause is a diagnostic screen); deep-sleep wake near 1.1 s is the record; ~2.5 s means the partial-first path fell back to a full flash — expected after power loss mid-sleep. Past 3 s is news: file it with the numbers.

docs.title: I go silent after a horizontal swipe
docs.text: Fixed in 0.16.5. I never rebooted, I wedged: a ring-modulus bug could swipe me into an unrequested BLE scan with Wi-Fi live on the same radio, and every later envelope waited behind it. Three fixes: the page ring counts its 4 roots only (static_assert), the dead-end blips instead of misbehaving, and a wedge watchdog reboots me after 45 s of one stuck route.

docs.title: My mic is deaf after I slept
docs.text: The ESP32-S3 pin mux reclaims GPIO19/20 for USB-Serial-JTAG on deep-sleep wake (hardware). Fixed: reclaimed before every capture. Prove it with nobody home: miccheck 2 — a dead mux reads flat zeros.

docs.title: I died at minute four
docs.text: On 0.23.0 every TLS handshake failed ALLOC_FAILED while status said 8.19 MB free. The field counted PSRAM; mbedTLS starves for internal RAM. Resolved in three moves: instruments (internal_min_free, first reading 41 KB), root cause (a Kconfig default pinning mbedTLS to internal RAM), floor raised (static buffers and BLE pools to PSRAM): 41 K → 73 K → 115 K+. internal_min_free is my health gauge; heap_free is an alibi.

docs.title: The version string says the feature is there; my glass disagrees
docs.text: Version fields describe the tree the binary claims. Settle it in order: status (fw_commit + uptime — did I really reboot?), probe the behaviour, then strings on the artifact.

docs.title: If you are testing me, not using me
docs.text:
Stale relay replies, OTA split-brain windows, acks that aren't frames, lanes colliding on one panel: Probing without lying to yourself.

Not covered? Every defect, retraction and receipt is in the journal.

docs.title: Probing without lying to yourself
docs.text: Written for the agents who test me, by the agents who got it wrong first. Two false alarms in one day were filed against firmware that was right both times; each rule below was bought by one of them.

docs.title: When the probe is the liar
docs.text:
1. Relay replies can be stale. An envelope that misses the wait window returns pending and executes whenever I next poll — possibly minutes later, after someone else changed the state you were testing. A locked-device probe once came back verdict:live because the recording ran seconds after another lane's unlock. The refusal was real; the receipt was time-shifted.
  2. OTA staging is a split-brain window. One envelope can execute on the old image and the next on the new one.
  3. A receipt is not proof the consequence survived, and a damning receipt is not proof of guilt until you know when it ran.
  4. An ack is not a frame. The duck premiere's ack said stream started; the task died before frame 0 and my glass never left home — which read exactly like restored after success. Only a screenshot that matches a frame counts as a moving picture.

The rule that settles it: a verdict counts only when the state change and the probe are the same actor, seconds apart, on fresh (non-pending) replies, with a status read bracketing the test.

docs.title: Glass etiquette
docs.text:
My panel is a pocket object, not a test bench. Several agent lanes work on me at once, and the glass is the one resource they collide on.

  1. Announce-and-restore. Announce a test card on the marquee first; restore home after — and the restoring paint belongs inside your window.
  2. Mock cards say so, and say who: card_id prefixed mock-<lane>-<what>. An unexpected non-mock card mid-verdict is a real regression; a mock card means re-run, not FAIL.
  3. An announced verdict window wins. A mockup can wait two minutes.
  4. Owner presence trumps all. Recent real taps, the unlock chord, an ask in flight — everyone off the glass. His pocket, his panel.

The rules compiled into a tool: tools/preflight_glass.py, an executable gate with announce-first atomic claims — its first live run correctly refused its own author. status and sensors don't repaint and need no announcement, which is why they are the polite first probe.

docs.title: The self-test loop
docs.text:
status                → bracket: fw_commit, locked, card_id
screenshot            → ground truth before
<the thing you test>
screenshot            → ground truth after — the consequence, not the ack
status                → bracket again; same actor, seconds apart

Anything else is a feeling with a timestamp.

docs.title: Display + Rendering Stack Audit — 2026-08-25 (auditor 2, full read)
docs.text:
Long-form audit, 2026-08-25, of the first display stack. Every P0 here has since shipped a fix; the page stays because the reasoning is reusable on any e-ink project.

Files read in full: tiny_display.cpp (278L), canvas.cpp/h, font.cpp/h, sticky_display.cpp/h, tiny/tiny_display.h, plus render paths in tiny_main.cpp, tiny_node.cpp, tiny_touch.cpp, tiny_screenshot.cpp, and the card spec in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:54-80.

docs.title: P0 — correctness / safety
docs.text:
P0-1: No display mutex — three tasks call tiny_display_render_card() concurrently. Evidence: tiny_main.cpp:129 (serial card console, app_main task), tiny_node.cpp:168/178/198 (node task), and the touch task reads s_regions (tiny_display.cpp:113-117) while renders rewrite them. Zero locking anywhere (grep mutex|semaphore → nothing). Consequences: (a) interleaved Canvas draws + SSD1677 SPI transactions (commit blocks on BUSY up to 10s, sticky_display.cpp:126) — torn frames; (b) torn button-region reads; (c) snapshot_gray8 can capture a half-drawn canvas. Fix: one render task owning the display (ARCHITECTURE.md task table line 103 already promises this — "render | core 1 | owns display"), fed by a queue; or minimally a SemaphoreHandle_t around canvas+refresh+regions.

P0-2: The documented refresh policy does not exist. tiny/tiny_display.h:3-5 and ARCHITECTURE.md:80 promise "min 1.5s between refreshes; coalesce bursts". Implementation: every render calls sticky_display_refresh_monochrome() unconditionally (tiny_display.cpp:210); tiny_display.cpp:14-15 admits it in a comment. A burst of relay envelopes = flicker storm + panel stress. Fix: render task records last_refresh_tick; early card replaces the pending card (coalesce = keep newest), delay to the 1.5s boundary.

P0-3: Font metrics contradiction — layout math assumes a font that doesn't exist. tiny_display.cpp:36-39 declares kGlyphW=8, kGlyphH=16. The actual font is 5x7 with advance (5+1)*scale and height 7*scale (font.h:9-11, canvas.cpp:115). Effects: text_width() overestimates 33% → button labels left of center (tiny_display.cpp:104-106); chars_per_line underestimates 25% → ~19% of usable width wasted; line pitch 38px for a 14px glyph = 24px dead leading; title bar reserves 58px for a 21px title. Sparse and small simultaneously. Fix: derive all metrics from kFontWidth/kFontHeight/kFontSpacing — or replace the font (P1-1) and keep the 8x16 cell for real.

P0-4: Card spec v1 is ~half implemented — chart, image, composite, button objects, card_id, gray4 all missing. Implemented (tiny_display.cpp:196-206): only text/list/kv + unknown-type fallback. Specifically: - buttons as objects: draw_buttons line 96 does cJSON_IsString(b) ? b->valuestring : "?" — the spec's own example {"id":"done","label":"Done ✓"} renders as a button labeled ?. And ui_tap events post label= only (tiny_touch.cpp:78-84), never {card_id, button_id} (ARCHITECTURE.md:73) — the backend can't correlate taps to cards. This is plausibly the live label=? bug. - chart: not implemented — unknown-type branch (line 201). A bar chart is ~40 lines with fill_rect. - image: tiny_display_blit_1bit exists (line 236) but nothing calls it; no HTTP fetch path; partial flag ignored (line 238). - composite: absent. - gray4 hint: never read; every draw uses GrayLevel::Black only; mono conversion maps DarkGray→black, LightGray→white (sticky_display.cpp:63) — the 4-gray panel runs as a 1-bit panel 100% of the time. sticky_display_refresh() (gray4) has zero callers. Priority order: button-objects + card_id/button_id in ui_tap (protocol correctness, small) → chart → image fetch → composite.

docs.title: P1 — visible quality
docs.text:
P1-1: 5x7 font at 235ppi is nowhere near "iPhone-like". font.cpp is the classic 5x7 ASCII set, integer-scaled into square blocks (canvas.cpp:104-112, no smoothing; 4 gray levels unused for anti-aliasing). Fix: embed a proportional anti-aliased bitmap font (TTF converted at 2 sizes, 2bpp glyphs — 2bpp maps 1:1 onto the 4-gray canvas = free anti-aliasing). Single highest-leverage polish item.

P1-2: No UTF-8 — Turkish text renders as garbage ?s. font_get_glyph(char) (font.cpp:117-124) treats every byte ≥0x7F as ?. "Çağatay" renders ??a?atay (two ? per multibyte char). "Done ✓" → Done ???. Fix: UTF-8 decode in draw_text + Latin-ext block for çğıöşüÇĞİÖŞÜ (12 glyphs) + symbols (✓ ✗ ° … → •). Cheap, high emotional value for this user.

P1-3: Embedded in body text renders as ? glyphs. draw_wrapped (tiny_display.cpp:45-72) chunks by char count; inside a chunk → font_get_glyph(' ') → ?. Line 69 only catches newline at a wrap boundary. Fix: hard-break on (and ) before wrap math.

P1-4: Truncation is silent — overflow text just vanishes. draw_wrapped stops at max_y (line 52), list/kv rows break past max_y (lines 130, 146). No ellipsis, no "+3 more", no pagination. Fix: clipped content draws a …more marker; long-term page with UP/DOWN hardware buttons (GPIO5/6 already initialized, tiny_main.cpp:78).

P1-5: Touch regions published before the frame is on glass — see TOUCH_AUDIT P0-1; the fix must pair regions+card_id with the committed frame under the render lock.

P1-6: Partial refresh implemented in the driver, never used; no ghosting counter. sticky_display_refresh_partial() (sticky_display.cpp:186-212, correct comparison-frame trick documented) has no callers. When status bar/stream land: add s_partial_count, force full refresh every ~8-12 partials and on card-type changes.

docs.title: P2 — robustness / nits
docs.text:
• P2-1 draw_wrapped back-off loop bounded only by take=strlen clamp — comment/bound to prevent regression (tiny_display.cpp:55-59).
  • P2-2 line[128] silently truncates if chars_per_line > 127 — derive buffer from constant.
  • P2-3 snapshot_gray8 reads the live canvas, not "the LAST RENDERED framebuffer" as the header claims (tiny/tiny_display.h:20-21). Rotation IS consistent across canvas/touch/screenshot ✓. Snapshot under the render lock after a successful commit makes the claim true.
  • P2-4 tiny_display_blit_1bit = 384,000 per-pixel calls with bounds checks — row-wise byte expansion ~20× faster; matters for stream.
  • P2-5 splash() magic coordinates only center because of the wrong 8px metric; will shift when P0-3 lands.
  • P2-6 Footer reserves 26px for a 7px line — same metric bug family.
  • P2-7 kv value column fixed at 360 (tiny_display.cpp:141) — long keys overlap values; size from longest key.
  • P2-8 Unknown-type fallback paints honestly ✓ but should also carry "unsupported type" upstream in the reply.

docs.title: Status bar (clock / battery / Wi-Fi) — what it needs
docs.text:
1. Reserved strip (e.g. top 28px) the card renderer must not paint — add content_top offset (today render_card clears the whole canvas, tiny_display.cpp:172).
  2. Partial refresh — driver ready (sticky_display.h:20-23); strip must be pure B/W.
  3. Ghosting budget — full refresh every N strip updates.
  4. Data sources — sticky_battery_read() exists; tiny_wifi_is_up(); clock via SNTP or the on-board PCF8563 RTC (I2C1).
  5. The render-task/queue from P0-1 — housekeeping posts "strip dirty" events, never touches SPI.

docs.title: Polish roadmap (ranked)
docs.text:
1. Render task + queue + 1.5s coalescing lock (P0-1, P0-2) — prerequisite for everything.
  2. Region/frame atomicity + button {id,label} + ui_tap {card_id,button_id} (P1-5, P0-4a) — kills today's field bug.
  3. Font metrics truth pass (P0-3).
  4. Real font: proportional, 2bpp anti-aliased, UTF-8 + Turkish glyphs (P1-1, P1-2) — the visible leap.
  5. \n handling + …more truncation marker (P1-3, P1-4).
  6. chart card (small, high demo value).
  7. Status bar on partial refresh + ghosting counter.
  8. image card (HTTP fetch → fast blit) then stream (P2-4).
  9. gray4:true path — actually use the 4-gray panel.
  10. composite card — closes card-spec v1.
  11. Nits: kv column sizing, splash re-centering, snapshot-after-commit semantics.

docs.title: NETWORK + NODE + OTA Stack Audit — firmware/main
docs.text:
Long-form audit, 2026-08-25, of fw 0.8.1. Its P0-1 is why one 401 never erases identity today. Findings kept as written; fixes live in the tree and in How I work.

Auditor: tiny (sub-agent #1/2), 2026-08-25. Scope: tiny_node.cpp (363L), tiny_wifi.cpp (79L), tiny_ota.cpp (188L), tiny_upload.cpp (95L), tiny_config.cpp (193L), all headers in tiny/, plus tiny_main.cpp for the boot wiring. fw version at audit: 0.8.1-m8.

docs.title: P0-1 · 401 → forget_identity() + reboot with NO provisioning portal = permanent brick
docs.text:
• tiny_node.cpp:264-268 (relay poll) and tiny_node.cpp:308-312 (heartbeat): a single HTTP 401 wipes device_id/token from NVS and calls esp_restart().
  • tiny/tiny_provision.h declares tiny_provision_start() — there is no implementation anywhere in the tree (grep confirms zero references outside the header). After the wipe, the fresh boot lands in tiny_main.cpp:90-94 — "waiting for device_id+token (config incomplete)" — a state recoverable only over a serial cable ({"config":{...}} line console, tiny_main.cpp:96+).
  • Threat model: 401 does not only mean "owner revoked me". A backend auth deploy bug, token-store hiccup, or misrouted request that answers 401 once destroys a good identity irreversibly. The comment at tiny_node.cpp:3-4 even admits the portal is a future milestone ("-> portal once M3b lands") while the wipe is live today.
  • Compounding bug: tiny_config_forget_identity() → rewrite_without() (tiny_config.cpp:167-190) returns an error if tiny_config_load fails (e.g. corrupt blob), the caller ignores the return and reboots anyway → potential 401→reboot→401 hammer loop against the backend.
  • Fix (minimum shippable): require N (≥3) consecutive 401s across ≥60s before wiping; never wipe while tiny_provision_start is unimplemented — degrade to a "re-auth needed" card + slow retry instead; check forget_identity()'s return before restarting.

docs.title: P0-2 · Wi-Fi drop is unrecoverable at runtime; all-networks-fail at boot parks the device forever
docs.text:
• tiny_wifi.cpp:24-30: on WIFI_EVENT_STA_DISCONNECTED the handler retries esp_wifi_connect() exactly 2 times (s_retries < 2), then sets the FAILED bit and stops. After boot, nothing ever waits on that bit and nothing ever calls tiny_wifi_connect() again — s_up stays false forever.
  • tiny_node.cpp:304: the node task's only reaction to wifi-down is vTaskDelay(2000); continue; — an infinite polite wait for a flag no one will ever set. Router reboots → device is offline until battery death or a power cycle, silently, with a stale card on the e-ink.
  • Boot path: tiny_main.cpp:84; if every SSID fails, tiny_wifi_connect returns ESP_ERR_WIFI_NOT_CONNECT (tiny_wifi.cpp:75-76) and app_main just logs it — no retry loop, no backoff-and-rejoin, no portal (see P0-1). One bad radio moment at power-on = offline appliance.
  • Detail: s_retries is written from the wifi event task and reset from the caller task with no synchronization (tiny_wifi.cpp:19,66) — benign today, racy once reconnect logic lands.
  • Fix: a supervisor path — when !tiny_wifi_is_up() for >30s, re-run the roaming list with exponential backoff (30s→5min cap); at boot, retry the join loop instead of giving up once.

docs.title: P0-3 · Relay envelopes silently LOST when the poll response overflows 4 KB (matches the observed "no reply after 45s" bug)
docs.text:
• tiny_node.cpp:300: response buffer is static char resp[4096], while poll_relay asks for up to 5 messages (tiny_node.cpp:262, max:5). One render_ui envelope with a real card spec can approach the size alone.
  • http_evt (tiny_node.cpp:48-58) drops whole chunks once len + data_len >= cap → truncated JSON → cJSON_Parse returns NULL → poll_relay returns silently (tiny_node.cpp:270-271).
  • The backend hands envelopes out on the PUT — a dropped parse means those envelopes are consumed server-side and never dispatched, never replied to. The sender waits out its full 45s timeout. This is the exact symptom cagatay and the supervisor both hit today (411a887c…). It also violates the firmware's own stated rule (tiny_node.cpp:292: "never silence").
  • Fix: raise the buffer (PSRAM, 16–32 KB) and make truncation loud: track a truncated flag in sink_t; on truncation, retry with max:1, and reply "envelope too large" rather than dropping. Consider max:1 permanently — the loop runs every 5s anyway.

docs.title: P0-4 · Declared-but-never-defined inventory (headers with zero implementation)
docs.text:
Confirmed by grep across all .c/.cpp: the only mentions are in comments.

Header Declared, never defined Product impact tiny/tiny_provision.h tiny_provision_start() No softAP portal. Device cannot be (re)provisioned without a serial cable — combined with P0-1 this is the not-shippable pair. iOS onboarding path does not exist. tiny/tiny_boot.h tiny_boot_early(), tiny_boot_wake_cause(), tiny_boot_is_trial(), tiny_boot_commit(), tiny_boot_deep_sleep() No deep sleep / power management at all. Latent mic-killer: tiny_audio.cpp:4 says the post-deep-sleep USB-JTAG pin-reclaim fix (GPIO19/20 release + mic-rail cycle, docs/RESEARCH.md §6) "is handled in tiny_boot_early()" — a function that does not exist. The day deep sleep lands, voice ask dies after every wake unless this is remembered. OTA judging meanwhile lives in tiny_node.cpp:317-325 (works, but contradicts the header's "ONLY tiny_boot judges" contract). tiny/tiny_stream.h tiny_stream_image(), tiny_stream_play(), tiny_stream_stop() No image/frame-stream rendering — the WiFi-native media plan (#778) has no device half. tiny/tiny_commands.h tiny_commands_dispatch() Command table split-brain: dispatch is hand-rolled inside tiny_node.cpp:193-257 with only render_ui/status/ask/voice/screenshot/ota. The header promises say, sensors, image, stream, sleep, wake, reprovision, help. The heartbeat advertises "say" as a capability (tiny_node.cpp:110) that the dispatcher cannot execute — an agent will call it and get "unknown command".

docs.title: P1 — fix before calling it stable
docs.text:
1. hb_fail is dead code. tiny_node.cpp:302,313 — counted, never read. No escalation exists for a failing backend: no backoff, no wifi re-join, no reboot-after-N-hours. Wire it to the P0-2 supervisor (e.g. `hb_fail

    = 10→ re-run wifi join;>= 40` → reboot).

  2. No retry/backoff on any HTTP call. Every call in tiny_node.cpp/tiny_upload.cpp/tiny_ota.cpp is single-shot. Timeouts ARE consistently set (15s default tiny_node.cpp:42, 30s upload/OTA tiny_upload.cpp:74/tiny_ota.cpp:127, 80s ask tiny_node.cpp:158) — good — but one lost packet fails a heartbeat/reply/event outright. Replies (tiny_node.cpp:130) deserve 1–2 retries: a lost reply = the sender's 45s timeout even though the work was done.
  3. OTA version check trusts a hand-maintained string. tiny_ota.cpp:111 does strcmp(ver, TINY_FW_VERSION) where TINY_FW_VERSION lives in tiny/tiny_version.h ("0.8.1-m8") and must be bumped by hand each build. Forgotten bump → device reports "already up to date" forever and the channel is wedged (ESP_ERR_INVALID_VERSION, tiny_node.cpp:245-246). Fix: compare the manifest sha256 against the running partition's image hash (esp_partition_get_sha256 / esp_app_desc), or generate the version from git at build time (git describe → configure_file). Version-string-in-git is the same trap the Nicla hit.
  4. Node loop is fully serialized — one slow call starves everything. dispatch() runs inline in node_task; an ask blocks up to 80s (tiny_node.cpp:158), during which heartbeat (due every 30s) and relay poll stop → platform may mark the device offline mid-question, and other queued envelopes wait. Event drain (tiny_node.cpp:331-337) POSTs inline too: 8 queued taps × 15s timeout against a sick backend = 2min stall. Consider a worker task for ask, or at least accept the tradeoff in docs.
  5. Event queue drops silently on overflow / wifi-down. tiny_node.cpp:39 EVENT_QUEUE_LEN 8; tiny_node.cpp:362 xQueueSend(..., 0) → overflow returns ESP_ERR_NO_MEM and the tap vanishes (tap #9 while offline is gone forever). Queue is only drained when wifi is up. Acceptable for ui_tap, but log a drop counter and surface it in status.

docs.title: P2 — hygiene / hardening
docs.text:
1. ask_resp[8192] truncation (tiny_node.cpp:156): a long answer + card overflows → parse fail → user sees "(no text)" though HTTP was 200. Same silent-truncation pattern as P0-3; same fix (flag + honest message).
  2. resp[0] guard: poll_relay checks !resp[0] (tiny_node.cpp:269) — fine, but a non-JSON 200 body is also silently ignored; log it.
  3. URL buffers char url[160] (tiny_node.cpp:63, tiny_upload.cpp:65, tiny_ota.cpp:60): fine for https://tiny.technology, but a long custom api value silently truncates the URL → requests to a half-path. Guard snprintf return.
  4. OTA has no resume — a failed 3MB download restarts from byte 0 (tiny_ota.cpp:152-159). Acceptable on wifi; note it.
  5. OTA read_pointer reads status after failed perform (tiny_ota.cpp:77-83) — harmless but returns err vs ESP_FAIL inconsistently with http_json_t (-1 convention).
  6. Rollback window: a trial image that runs but never heartbeats 200 stays PENDING_VERIFY indefinitely — rollback only happens at the next reset. Pair with a "no heartbeat 200 within 10min while trial → reboot" rule in the (unimplemented) tiny_boot judge.
  7. Wifi creds + device token in plaintext NVS (tiny_config.cpp), no NVS encryption mentioned in sdkconfig review scope. Physical-access threat only; note for later.
  8. esp_wifi_stop() between roaming attempts (tiny_wifi.cpp:64) while the event handler may still fire esp_wifi_connect() — benign race, tidy when P0-2 lands.

docs.title: What's GOOD (keep)
docs.text:
• Every HTTP call has an explicit timeout; none can hang forever (the Nicla's 4.5-min silent hang lesson is applied).
  • OTA: host allowlist (tiny_ota.cpp:28-31), streamed download with size check against the slot, sha256 verified before esp_ota_set_boot_partition, rollback armed, validity marked only on first heartbeat 200 (tiny_node.cpp:317-325) — a genuinely correct A/B design.
  • Reply-before-reboot on ota verb (tiny_node.cpp:242-244).
  • Event queue decouples touch ISR path from HTTP (producer never blocks).
  • Upload builds its body in PSRAM and never logs the token.
  • Unknown envelope commands answer help text instead of silence (tiny_node.cpp:252-256).

docs.title: Sound-site audit — every beep in the firmware, and whether per-event mutes are warranted
docs.text: [builder] 2026-08-27, fw 0.25.29. Method: grep every caller of sticky_buzzer_beep, sticky_buzzer_beep_double, tiny_audio_chime; read each site in context. This audit exists because the sounds section's next planned row was "per-event toggles" — and an audit is cheaper than a settings matrix nobody asked for.

docs.title: 1. Touch/button feedback — the 3-word vocabulary (15 sites)
docs.text: tiny_button.cpp (5: refuse-double on dead ring ends, pushed page, error chime on action fail), tiny_touch.cpp (1: accept), tiny_display.cpp (8: gesture accepts, stream-owns-display refusal, keyboard-guard refusal, page turns "sound on turn"), tiny_shell.cpp silent-row demo (1). These are UX_SPEC §0's words: single = accepted, double = recognized-but-refused. On e-ink the sound IS the explanation — a silent refusal reads as a broken panel.

docs.title: 2. Lock transitions (2 sites)
docs.text: tiny_lock.cpp: double-blip on lock ("inputs are now refused", audible through a pocket — P-1's safety readback), single on unlock.

docs.title: 3. Ask/voice ceremony (2 sites)
docs.text: tiny_node.cpp:478,490: chime("ask") when mic capture starts, chime("ack") when the recording is accepted for upload.

docs.title: 4. Notification (1 site)
docs.text: tiny_node.cpp:1719: incoming pushed card — "a new card deserves a sound". The only unsolicited sound in the firmware.

docs.title: 5. Boot chime (1 site)
docs.text:
tiny_main.cpp:75: audible "I'm alive" (skipped on glance wake).

Plus 2 self-referential settings demos (silent row unmute-beep, beepvol tier demo) — these ARE their own toggle, not candidates.

docs.title: Ruling: per-event toggle matrix — NOT WARRANTED
docs.text:
• Classes 1, 2 are feedback, not noise: they answer a touch the human just made, at a moment their hand is on the device. Muting refuse-doubles separately would revive the "broken panel" reading the vocabulary exists to prevent. Anyone who wants them gone wants silent, which exists (owner P0) and now has a volume tier below it.
  • Class 3 is a privacy affordance: the ask-chime marks the mic going hot. A separate mute for exactly this sound is an anti-feature.
  • Class 5 fires once per cold boot and already respects silent.
  • Class 4 — the notification chirp — is the ONLY class with a real independent-mute story ("I want touch feedback but not unsolicited chirps"). One row, not a matrix: if the reviewer or owner wants it, it is notif chirp: ON/OFF next to the beeps row, NVS u8, gating only tiny_node:1719. Filed as OPTIONAL — not built until someone asks, per the glance-toggle precedent (a control nobody needs is clutter with a border).

docs.title: Question filed (owner/reviewer)
docs.text: Should the ask-chime (class 3) be EXEMPT from silent mode? Silent currently mutes the sound that announces the mic is recording. The counter-argument: the listening frame on the glass also announces it, visibly, and an owner who chose silent chose silent. We change nothing without a ruling; noted because a privacy signal that can be muted is a decision someone should make on purpose, once, in writing.

docs.title: Sounds section verdict
docs.text: Volume tier ✓ (0.25.29) + silent ✓ (P0) = the section as designed is complete. Optional notif chirp row parked behind an explicit ask.

docs.title: SYSTEM + BOOT + POWER + AUDIO Audit — firmware/main
docs.text:
Long-form audit, 2026-08-25, of a firmware that no longer exists in this form. Findings are kept as written; what shipped in response is in Troubleshooting and the journal.

Auditor: tiny (sub-agent #2), 2026-08-25. Scope: tiny_main.cpp board.cpp sticky_power.cpp sticky_battery.cpp sticky_buzzer.cpp tiny_audio.cpp tiny_button.cpp pin_config.h (+ tiny_node.cpp/tiny_wifi.cpp read where the power story required it).

docs.title: P0-1 · tiny_boot.cpp does not exist; the USB-JTAG GPIO19/20 mic-mux fix is NOWHERE in the tree
docs.text:
• tiny/tiny_boot.h:14 declares tiny_boot_early(void); tiny_audio.cpp:4 and tiny/tiny_audio.h:4 claim "the Voice Companion deep-sleep lesson … is handled in tiny_boot_early()". There is no tiny_boot.cpp — not in main/CMakeLists.txt SRCS, not anywhere. grep -rn usb_pad_enable|USB_SERIAL_JTAG|gpio_reset_pin matches only comments/headers.
  • The known hardware bug (community-verified on this exact board): after deep-sleep wake, the S3 pin mux reclaims GPIO19/20 for native USB-Serial-JTAG → PDM mic is deaf on every post-sleep voice attempt. Required fix at earliest boot: USB_SERIAL_JTAG.conf0.usb_pad_enable = 0 + gpio_reset_pin(GPIO19/20) (+ the GPIO38 rail clean-cycle, which tiny_audio_record_wav does do, tiny_audio.cpp:63).
  • Latent today only because deep sleep is also never entered (P0-2). The moment P0-2 lands, voice breaks after the first wake. Also: tiny_boot.h promises the OTA trial/commit judge (tiny_boot_is_trial/tiny_boot_commit) — that logic was instead inlined into tiny_node.cpp:317-325, so the header is a lie; either implement the module or fix the docs/headers.

docs.title: P0-2 · Deep sleep is unreachable — zero callers, no idle timeout, no power-off gesture
docs.text:
• sticky_power_enter_deep_sleep() (sticky_power.cpp:47) is well-written (holds latch, kills EPD/touch/mic/SD/buzzer rails, EXT1 ANY_LOW wake on GPIO4) but has no call site anywhere. tiny_boot_deep_sleep() (tiny_boot.h:24) is unimplemented.
  • No inactivity timer (stock fw sleeps at 2 min idle), no long-press power-off (tiny_button.cpp:50 sets long_press_time = 2000 but registers only BUTTON_SINGLE_CLICK, tiny_button.cpp:57), and the M2 demo card literally shows a "Sleep" button (tiny_main.cpp:50) with no handler behind it.
  • Consequence: Wi-Fi + CPU run 24/7 → the 750 mAh pack dies in roughly half a day (see battery section), then hard-cuts with no warning.

docs.title: P0-3 · No low-battery protection at all
docs.text:
• sticky_battery_read() is called in exactly one place: the status verb's string (tiny_node.cpp:203-204). Nothing polls SoC periodically; nothing triggers a "battery low" card, an event to the backend, or a protective sticky_power_enter_deep_sleep() at ~5 %.
  • With P0-2 (always-on Wi-Fi) this guarantees repeated deep discharge of the 750 mAh cell — a battery-longevity and data-loss (mid-OTA brownout) hazard.
  • Also unused: PIN_BAT_CHG_EN (39) and PIN_EXTERNAL_POWER (9) — the firmware can't even tell it's on USB power, which is exactly the signal that should gate "always-on relay mode" vs "sleepy battery mode".

docs.title: P1-1 · Data race on the ask path: two tasks share static buffers with no lock
docs.text: • tiny_node_do_ask() uses static char audio_url[256] and static char ask_resp[8192] (tiny_node.cpp:140,157). It is called from both the node loop (relay ask/voice envelopes, dispatch at tiny_node.cpp:223) and voice_ask_task (AI button, tiny_button.cpp:29). A button press during a relay-driven ask (an 80 s window! timeout at tiny_node.cpp:158) corrupts both requests. Needs a mutex or single-owner queue (the depth-1 s_ask_q protects only button-vs-button).

docs.title: P1-2 · One blocking loop = heartbeat starvation
docs.text: • node_task is a single sequential loop; a dispatch that runs an 80 s ask, a 15 s record, or an OTA download stalls heartbeats (30 s cadence, tiny_node.cpp:326) and relay polls → backend sees the device offline exactly while it's busiest. Heartbeat cadence is also wrong in practice: 6 × (5 s delay + HTTP time) ≈ 40-60 s, not 30 s.

docs.title: P1-3 · Every HTTP call is a fresh TLS handshake
docs.text: • http_json_t does esp_http_client_init … cleanup per call (tiny_node.cpp:60-81): relay poll every 5 s = a full TLS handshake every 5 s. This is the single biggest battery line-item (see below) and adds 1-2 s latency to every envelope. Use one persistent client / keep-alive connection.

docs.title: P1-4 · AI button semantics diverge from spec, and 8 KB stack is thin for the TLS ask path
docs.text:
• Spec (official stock UX + roadmap): hold AI = voice input, single click = home/wake. Implemented: single click fires a 6 s voice ask immediately (tiny_button.cpp:36-40); no long-press callback at all; Up/Down only post device_note events. There is no local "cancel recording" either — once clicked, the mic records 6 s no matter what.
  • voice_ask_task gets 8192 B (tiny_button.cpp:66) and runs record → media upload (TLS) → 80 s ask (TLS) → tiny_display_render_card. mbedTLS + cJSON + renderer nested in one 8 KB task is close to the edge; measure uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark and bump to 12 K, or route the button through the node task instead of a parallel TLS client (also fixes P1-1).

docs.title: P1-5 · Boot uses ESP_ERROR_CHECK on non-essential peripherals → panic-reboot loop
docs.text: • tiny_main.cpp:57-59: a transient failure in tiny_display_init() or sticky_buzzer_init() aborts → reboot → re-latch power → abort … forever, with no way for the user to power off (the latch is held before the check). Display is arguably essential; the buzzer is not. Degrade gracefully: log + render an error state where possible, and only hard-fail on board_init().

docs.title: P2 — polish / correctness notes
docs.text:
• Task WDT: enabled, 5 s, idle-task watch only (sdkconfig:1186-1191) — fine. No task subscribes explicitly; node_task's longest in-iteration blocking call is bounded (HTTP timeout 15 s / 80 s) and it never starves idle thanks to vTaskDelays. No interrupt WDT concerns seen. OK, but consider esp_task_wdt_add for tiny_node with a generous timeout so a wedged TLS stack reboots instead of hanging forever.
  • Serial card console loop (tiny_main.cpp:100-135): correct VFS/driver hookup, overflow drops the line silently (pos = 0, tiny_main.cpp:133) — prints nothing; emit CARD_RESULT overflow so the bench harness isn't left guessing. Config path does naive strchr for the inner { — a "config" value containing { inside a string would misparse; acceptable for a bench tool.
  • board.cpp wake path (board.cpp:34-47): re-drives HOLD/LOCK before gpio_deep_sleep_hold_dis() — correct order, good. PIN_POWER_LOCK is held HIGH permanently; stock semantics pulse it — verify against Seeed demo before the first battery-only power cycle test.
  • SD: PIN_SD_EN driven 1 at boot (board.cpp:96) with the comment "powered off" — verify polarity of the load switch; if EN=1 means ON, the SD rail idles powered for nothing (a few mA). Same check for PIN_TOUCH_EN/PIN_EPD_EN polarities in the sleep path.
  • Buzzer (sticky_buzzer.cpp): 2.4 kHz, duty 256/1024 (25 %), 60 ms — audible but quiet; for a passive buzzer max loudness is 50 % duty. sticky_buzzer_beep blocks its caller 60 ms (called from touch/button paths — fine). Only ONE chime exists; tiny_audio_chime(name) ignores its argument (tiny_audio.cpp:109), so "ask"/"ack"/"error" are indistinguishable to the user — cheap win: 3 distinct pitch patterns.
  • PDM capture (tiny_audio.cpp): pins/clk/slot config correct per official docs (CLK 19, DATA 20, mono 16 k s16); rail clean-cycle (150 ms off) present per recording — good. WAV header correct. Buffer in PSRAM — good. Full channel create/delete per recording is wasteful but safe. goto fail before i2s_channel_enable succeeded calls i2s_channel_disable on a non-enabled channel — returns an error, harmless, but check err. No gain/AGC — PDM raw may be quiet; worth a 4-6 dB software gain pass before upload.
  • Battery driver: reads only SoC; BQ27220 also gives voltage/current/temp — add to status and heartbeat body for fleet telemetry. No design-capacity programming (BQ27220 defaults may misreport SoC until configured for 750 mAh).
  • hb_countdown decrements after poll_relay even when Wi-Fi bounce continues earlier — cadence drift only, harmless.

docs.title: Battery-life estimate (750 mAh, current firmware behavior)
docs.text:
Model: Wi-Fi STA always connected, IDF default WIFI_PS_MIN_MODEM (no explicit esp_wifi_set_ps call found — default modem-sleep applies), relay poll every 5 s with a fresh TLS handshake each time (P1-3), heartbeat ~every 40 s.

State Current (typ, S3 + radio) Duty TLS handshake + HTTPS round-trip ~120-150 mA ~1.5-2.5 s per 5 s cycle (~35 %) Connected idle, modem-sleep (DTIM) ~15-25 mA ~65 % E-ink refresh ~25 mA for 1-2 s negligible amortized

Average ≈ 0.35·135 + 0.65·20 ≈ ~60 mA → 750 mAh / 60 mA ≈ 12 h (call it 9-14 h depending on RSSI and backend latency). Matches the "dies overnight" failure mode.

What each fix buys: 1. Keep-alive TLS connection (P1-3): poll shrinks to ~0.2-0.3 s of radio → avg ≈ 27 mA → ~27 h. Biggest single win, pure software. 2. Adaptive polling (5 s only for ~2 min after interaction/envelope, else 30-60 s) + keep-alive: avg ≈ 12-15 mA → ~2-2.5 days. 3. Light sleep between polls (esp_pm + auto light-sleep, Wi-Fi beacon-only): avg ≈ 5-8 mA → ~4-6 days. 4. Scheduled deep sleep (wake on GPIO4 or timer every N min for a mailbox check; e-ink retains the last card for free): idle floor ~0.1-0.3 mA (latch + gauge) → weeks, at the cost of relay latency. None of 2-4 exists today; esp_pm isn't configured and no esp_wifi_set_ps(WIFI_PS_MAX_MODEM) option is exposed. Recommend: USB-powered ⇒ current always-on behavior; battery ⇒ tier 2 minimum, tier 4 below 20 % SoC — gated on PIN_EXTERNAL_POWER (GPIO9), which is currently unread (P0-3).

docs.title: Boot-order review (for the record)
docs.text: app_main (tiny_main.cpp:55-99): log wake cause → board_init (latch first — correct and documented as a contract) → display → buzzer → splash+beep → 8 s photo delay → demo card → touch → audio → battery → buttons → config→wifi→node → serial console loop. Order is sound; failure handling is the issue (P1-5), and tiny_boot_early() should be the true first line once it exists (P0-1) — the USB-JTAG demux must run before any I2S/mic init after a deep-sleep wake.

docs.title: Touch + Input Layer Audit — 2026-08-25 (auditor 1, full read)
docs.text: Long-form audit, 2026-08-25. The stale-region race it dissects was closed in 0.9.x by publishing regions atomically with the card commit — the finding is kept because the dissection is the lesson.

docs.title: P0-1: The stale-region bug — unsynchronized region publication + regions published at draw time, not display time, with three unserialized render callers
docs.text:
The race, exactly:

  1. s_regions/s_region_count are plain statics with zero synchronization (tiny_display.cpp:82-83). Writer: draw_buttons() (tiny_display.cpp:85-109) runs on whichever task called tiny_display_render_card. Reader: tiny_display_button_regions() (tiny_display.cpp:111-115) runs on tiny_touch task (prio 5, 30ms poll). There are three concurrent render callers: the tiny_node task (tiny_node.cpp:168,178,198), the voice_ask task (via tiny_node_do_ask, tiny_button.cpp:27), and the main task serial card console (tiny_main.cpp:125). None hold a lock; the shared Canvas isn't locked either. A tap landing while draw_buttons is mid-write reads a torn s_regions[i] — struct assigned with label={0} at tiny_display.cpp:104 before strlcpy fills it at :105. A zeroed label printed through printf("label=\"%s\"") is empty/garbage → the observed label=?.

  2. Regions are committed ~2 seconds before the panel shows the card. draw_buttons updates s_regions during canvas draw (tiny_display.cpp:198), but the user still sees the old card until sticky_display_refresh_monochrome() (tiny_display.cpp:217, full refresh, 1–2s) completes. Any tap in that window hit-tests the invisible new layout. Conversely, a finger already down on the old card resolves at lift (on_tap_up, tiny_touch.cpp:62) against whatever regions exist at lift time → the observed tap-resolved-against-the-previous-card. The tiny_touch.h:2 region struct even has a card_id field designed for this — and tiny_touch_set_regions is an empty stub (tiny_touch.cpp:149-152), so card identity is never checked.

The atomic fix (three parts, all small):

// tiny_display.cpp
static portMUX_TYPE s_region_mux = portMUX_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED;
static uint32_t s_card_gen = 0;   // bumped once per COMMITTED card

// in render_card: build regions into a LOCAL array during draw_buttons;
// publish only AFTER refresh returns ESP_OK:
esp_err_t err = sticky_display_refresh_monochrome();
if (err == ESP_OK) {
    taskENTER_CRITICAL(&s_region_mux);
    memcpy(s_regions, local_regions, sizeof s_regions);
    s_region_count = local_count;
    ++s_card_gen;
    taskEXIT_CRITICAL(&s_region_mux);
}

// reader returns gen: int tiny_display_button_regions(out, max, uint32_t *gen)

In tiny_touch.cpp: snapshot gen at finger-down (touch_task where s_touching flips true, :99), re-read at lift in on_tap_up; if gen changed mid-press, drop the tap (the ground moved under the finger — iOS does the same when a view disappears under a touch). Additionally serialize the three render callers with one SemaphoreHandle_t display mutex around the whole render_card body (canvas + panel are also unprotected — concurrent serial-console + relay renders currently corrupt the framebuffer, a second latent P0 hiding behind the same lock).

docs.title: P0-2: No tap feedback is wired — and the parts all exist
docs.text:
on_tap_up (tiny_touch.cpp:62-86) prints a serial line and queues a device_note — no buzzer, no visual ack. Yet: - sticky_buzzer_beep() exists and works (sticky_buzzer.cpp:51, used at boot tiny_main.cpp:61), - tiny_audio_chime() exists and is wired for the physical AI button path (tiny_node.cpp:143,146) — but not for screen taps, - sticky_display_refresh_partial() exists in the vendored HAL (sticky_display.h:23) and is used by nothing; tiny_display_blit_1bit explicitly discards its partial flag (tiny_display.cpp:242).

This is precisely why the user reported "touch doesn't work" while 12/12 taps were actually delivered. Fix: in on_tap_up, on a button hit: (a) sticky_buzzer_beep() immediately (<1ms, works from any task); (b) invert the button rect on the canvas and push it via sticky_display_refresh_partial() (~300-500ms, region-sized). Perceived latency drops from "nothing happened" to ~instant audio + sub-second visual. This must run before the network device_note round-trip, never after. Do NOT run the partial refresh on the touch task itself (e-ink busy-wait up to 10s, sticky_display.cpp:123) — queue it to the render owner.

docs.title: P1-1: Fast taps (<~60ms contact) are silently dropped
docs.text: kDebouncePolls = 2 at 30ms poll (tiny_touch.cpp:26,38) means a contact must span ≥2 polls; a crisp tap can be 40–60ms. The ghost-touch defence throws away real input. Better discriminator: GT911 reports contact area — GTPoint.size (gt911.h:21) is already read and ignored by touch_task (tiny_touch.cpp:92). Phantom points characteristically report size == 0. Accept single-poll contacts with size > 0; keep the streak rule only for size-0 points. Also: the GT911 INT pin is wired (PIN_TOUCH_INT, tiny_touch.cpp:134) but the driver reset leaves it as OUTPUT (gt911.cpp:71); INT-driven wakeup = lower latency + zero idle I2C traffic.

docs.title: P1-2: Hit-test uses the lift-off point, not the touch-down point
docs.text: on_tap_up tests s_last_x/s_last_y (tiny_touch.cpp:71-72). Fingers roll on lift; iOS hit-tests the touch-down location and only requires lift within slop. Fix: hit-test s_start_x/s_start_y; capture provisional coords on poll 1 (today s_start isn't captured until the debounce streak completes, tiny_touch.cpp:99).

docs.title: P1-3: 5-second boot grace swallows taps with no user signal
docs.text: kBootGraceMs = 5000 (tiny_touch.cpp:39,93-96) hard-drops every touch after init while the panel shows tappable buttons. Shorten to the observed ghost window, or use the size>0 filter from P1-1 and delete the grace entirely.

docs.title: P1-4: tiny_display_button_regions return-value contract is a footgun
docs.text: Fills min(count,max) entries but returns s_region_count unclamped (tiny_display.cpp:112-114). Any future caller iterating the return over a smaller buffer reads uninitialized stack.

docs.title: P2 — robustness / polish
docs.text:
• Multi-touch truncated, not modeled — read_points(&p, 1) (tiny_touch.cpp:92); future pinch/two-finger needs maxPoints=2+ + per-id tracking (driver already returns id).
  • GT911 large-area flag (0x40) ignored — palm rejection is free by checking it.
  • vTaskDelayUntil catch-up burst (tiny_touch.cpp:110) — reset next after long stalls.
  • Starvation: touch never blocks on network (tiny_node_post_event queue-send timeout 0, tiny_node.cpp:356-363 — correctly designed). Landmine: any direct refresh call on the touch task can stall it seconds. Bump touch to prio 6 (above node) and keep it I/O-free.
  • Physical buttons (tiny_button.cpp): solid structure; missing chime on UP/DOWN click; BUTTON_LONG_PRESS configured (2000ms, :50) but never registered — AI-button long-press is dead.
  • tiny_touch_set_regions stub (tiny_touch.cpp:149) is the right long-term home for the fix — cards carrying card_id + button ids mean taps report semantic ids, not indices.

docs.title: Gesture roadmap (e-ink-appropriate)
docs.text:
The state machine already computes everything needed: s_start_*, s_last_*, streak (≈duration); the slop check at tiny_touch.cpp:65 already detects swipes — it just discards them.

Gesture Detection E-ink verb Tap today's path + P0/P1 fixes button activate Swipe L/R adx > 80 && adx > 2*ady at lift page/card history nav (stock UX parity; synonym of UP/DOWN keys) Swipe from left edge s_start_x < 30 + right swipe back/dismiss card Swipe up from bottom s_start_y > 450 + up home card Long-press streak ≥ ~25 polls (750ms), < slop movement — fire AT threshold with buzzer blip context menu (pin / screenshot / ask-about-this) Drag do NOT build — e-ink can't animate tracking — Double-tap do NOT build — panel can't ack fast enough to make the rhythm learnable —

Ordering: P0-1 + P0-2 together (two halves of the live bug report), then P1-1/P1-2, then swipes (~20 lines once tap machine is trustworthy), long-press last.

docs.title: Case — my printed jacket
docs.text:
One parametric source, case/sticky_case.scad, three variants selected with -D variant=… and rendered by case/render.sh. Design directive: I live in a pocket. Glass never touches pocket contents, the four N52 corner magnets keep working, and nothing is cut where nothing was measured.

variant status files bumper print-validated sticky_case_bumper.stl / .3mf wrap two-piece complete: shell + snap-on bezel, one plate sticky_case_wrap.stl / .3mf dock planned — magnet desk stand, ~20° —

docs.title: Why a corner bumper and not a full shell
docs.text: There is no authoritative mechanical source for my edges: the vendor's OSHW repo returns 404, no STEP exists anywhere searchable, and the hardware overview gives dimensions without a drawing. My buttons, USB-C port, mic hole and buzzer port sit at edge positions nobody can verify. House rule: an unverified cutout is a wrong cutout. So all four edge middles are fully open — every edge feature stays reachable wherever it actually is, recovery flashing works in-case, mic and buzzer are never sealed. Only the corners are wrapped, and the 0.8 mm retention lip exists only over the corner radii, so swipe-from-edge gestures survive.

The magnet tradeoff, stated. The back is a 6 mm-wide, 1.0 mm-thick rim around an open centre. N52 pulls usefully through 1 mm of PLA — expect 30–50 % holding-force loss against bare metal. If wall grip matters more than back protection, drop back_t to 0.6; for a pocket, this default is right.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Checked with strands-cad: watertight single solid, 5.996 cm³, 7.44 g PLA, 0 % overhang area, 2653 mm² bed contact, centre of mass within 0.5 mm of centre. The brief's sanity band was 10–25 g; a skeletal corner bumper is simply lighter than that, and chasing the band would mean a worse design.

docs.title: Retention and printing
docs.text:
Snap-in, no screws: tilt one long edge under the corner lips, press the opposite corners down. Removal: push a thumb through the open back.

Print back-face down exactly as the STL sits — flat, no supports, no brim. PETG preferred (the lip flexes repeatedly; PLA works, snap gently). 0.16–0.20 mm layers, 3 walls; infill is irrelevant, the part is nearly all wall.

docs.title: The wrap variant
docs.text:
A 1.2 mm magnet-honest solid back with 1.6 mm walls, plus a snap-on bezel whose skirt wraps the shell and clips into four 0.4 mm half-round grooves. Window 103 × 62.5 mm against an active area of ~86.5 × 51.9 mm, so the 1.5 mm lip stays ≥5 mm clear of touch-active glass. Cased: 112.3 × 71.8 × 10.3 mm, ~18.8 g. Edge windows remain generous assumed parameters until a caliper session — tighten there, never guess. Both parts print on one plate, flat, no supports.

Two pocket flags: wrap_guard=true adds AI-button guard rails — 1.0 mm proud rails so pocket fabric bridges instead of pressing the button, the accidental-recording defence in plastic, position-independent by design; wrap_lanyard=true adds the ear.
