docs.title: Dashboard — sticky.cagatay.my
docs.text:
Long-form. The dashboard's own engineering ledger: architecture, every panel, every rail, every incident. If you only want to drive a Sticky, Commands is enough.

A remote-control cockpit for the Sticky: device status, live screen mirror, a render_ui composer, action buttons and an activity feed — served behind a WebAuthn passkey gate at https://sticky.cagatay.my (Cloudflare Tunnel sticky, backend on localhost:8787).

Code lives in docs/dashboard/: FastAPI backend (server.py) + React/Vite SPA (frontend/), launched by run.sh.

docs.title: How it controls the device
docs.text:
The Sticky is not on a LAN socket — it's controlled through the tiny.technology device relay:

sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Browser (passkey)
    participant D as Dashboard backend
    participant T as tiny.technology
    participant S as Sticky
    B->>D: POST /api/invoke {command}
    D->>T: POST /api/devices/relay {toDevice, payload:{type:"invoke",prompt}}
    T-->>D: {id: "env_…"}
    S->>T: PUT /api/devices/relay (5s poll)
    T-->>S: envelope
    S->>T: PATCH /api/devices/relay (reply)
    D->>T: GET /api/devices/relay?inReplyTo=env_…
    T-->>D: reply {result, images?}
    D-->>B: result

Two credentials, two directions:

  • the backend authenticates to tiny.technology as the owner — the same Bearer credential the tiny CLI writes to ~/.tiny/credentials.json (override: TINY_CREDENTIALS)
  • the browser authenticates to the backend with a passkey — WebAuthn (Touch ID / Face ID); the private key never leaves the secure enclave, the backend stores only the public key (.sticky_auth.json, chmod 600)

The async contract mirrors use_device: an invoke waits up to 45 s, then returns {pending, envelope_id}; GET /api/result/{envelope_id} redeems the reply later (the relay mailbox keeps it ~24 h). Image URLs in replies pass the same plugin.tiny.technology/media/* allowlist the tiny agents apply.

docs.title: Live mode — the real fridge panel
docs.text:
STICKY_MOCK=0 STICKY_DEVICE=sticky ./run.sh          # what runs today

Live mode is the production mode. The rules it plays by (fw 0.14.18-m12) — every one of them exists because the first live attempt lied on screen:

thing how live mode handles it status reply shape since 0.9.x the firmware answers machine-readable JSON (fw, battery_pct, charging, wifi, ssid, rssi_dbm, heap_free, psram_free, + a human summary field). parse_status() still accepts the older English sentence and reports which shape it saw; absent fields render as —, never as a guess. GET /api/status is the normalized route. screen mirror the screenshot verb uploads the framebuffer and answers with a hosted URL in the reply text (screenshot: https://plugin.tiny.technology/media/…png), not in images[]. The backend extracts it, checks it against is_device_media_url, and proxies the bytes at the guarded /api/screen.png — so the mirror is the REAL panel and the media URL never has to be exposed to the browser. 🎬 premiere ceremony POST /api/frames/<seq>/premiere — the entire stream-acceptance liturgy in one call: firmware-eye transport probe → announced glass window → play → player testimony → screenshot frame-matched against the rail's own previews (PIL greyscale diff, <5 % convicts) → home restore → window close. Every stage lands in the report even on failure — the ceremony is the anti-invisible-failure design generalized. Acceptance receipts: the frame-match convicted a known preview at 0.0 %, and the premiere gate correctly 409'd against the builder's live window — the etiquette held against its own author's tooling ⏳ premiere-when-free the one-slot queue that resolves etiquette's last tension: the builder re-opens windows faster than TTLs expire, so polite yielding must not mean the act never happens. Queue a sequence; the server polls the glass gate every 20 s for up to 30 min and fires the full receipted ceremony the moment the glass is free (double-queue = 409). Waiting is now infrastructure, not a lane's patience 🗂 sequence shelf GET /api/frames/library + a FramesCard in the SPA — every dithered sequence as thumbnails with a one-click 🎬 premiere that fires the ceremony and renders its stage receipts ⚠ heap instruments the 0.23.2 P0 gauges surfaced where eyes actually are: internal_free / min-watermark / last_boot on the status card, with a ⚠ badge when the low-water mark drops under 48 KiB. Its first live reading — 37.9 KiB, already in the danger band — is what turned the minute-four post-mortem into a live remediation (see troubleshooting) pocket controls a PocketRow on the Fleet card — 🔒 lock / 🔓 unlock / 👁 glance, buttons lit from the advertised-verbs handshake and etiquette-gated like every glass verb. Its acceptance run was this lane's first-ever paint on the real glass, done by its own rules: window announced on the marquee, glance run (receipt: partial refresh, battery 100 %, wifi ✓, unread 0, unlocked), home restored, window closed click-anywhere mirror beyond the derived button boxes: any pixel of the mirror is a real coordinate tap — offsetX/offsetY read in the element's pre-transform local space, so the mapping survives the ⟳ rotation the container applies (the same runtime-state discipline, applied to the browser's side of the glass). And tap/scroll/swipe joined GLASS_VERBS: a synthetic finger mid-premiere is as destructive as a paint, so the etiquette gate now covers input, not just output clickable mirror the relay cannot read the panel's current card back, so the backend remembers the last card spec it sent and derives button boxes with the firmware's own geometry (800×480, margin 24, 56 px bar at the bottom, gap 16, n≤4 split evenly — pixel-verified against a device screenshot). clicking a button a click cannot press the glass. It is logged as sim_tap and labelled "simulated" in the feed and in the UI. Real taps come from the device: the firmware posts them as device_note ui_tap button=N label=…, and the backend reads them owner-side from GET /api/events, showing them as ui_tap (source device). Tap zones whose id/label the firmware itself will act on (the action_for() sniff — m: rows, rescan wifi, …) are badged ⚡ with a dashed outline, and the tooltip says exactly what a real finger would also trigger; report-only zones stay clean. The badge runs the same deviceActionFor mirror as the composer lint — one truth, two surfaces. verbs the firmware lacks wake, reprovision, image, stream are refused with HTTP 501 + the reason, and their Action buttons are greyed out with that reason. An action that does nothing is a lie on the screen. slow envelopes every relay call runs in a threadpool (run_in_threadpool), so a 60 s pending invoke never freezes the dashboard — and a pending envelope is tracked, not dropped — and since the reaper went autonomous, redemption no longer depends on a browser being open: the registry persists to disk on every mutation (a launchd respawn mid-deploy no longer orphans in-flight envelopes), and a startup task polls every 20 s only while envelopes are in flight, blanket-caught so the reaper never dies. A late reply still lands in the feed (marked ↩), a late render_ui still updates the mirror's card truth, a late screenshot still updates the mirror image. After 15 min unanswered it's logged as expired (⌛) — abandoned visibly, never silently. In-flight envelopes are surfaced in /api/activity and as a banner. The original design redeemed only on activity polls — which meant owner out, late replies rot; that gap was found by its own fixtures (chart envelopes orphaned by a respawn) and closed.

Verbs that actually exist (fw 0.20.0-m14, twenty, all advertised): render_ui <card-json>, status, sensors [card], say <text>, ask <text>, voice [secs], screenshot, glance, miccheck [secs], page <nav>, rotate [deg|auto], tap <x> <y>, swipe <x1> <y1> <x2> <y2>, scroll [up|down|top|±px], lock, unlock, sleep [secs], ota [channel], messages [unread|thread <login>], play <manifest-url> | stop | status — the verb-by-verb reference is Commands. The five that arrived after this page's original audit (swipe in caps, lock/unlock at 0.17.0, glance at 0.18.0, play at 0.19.1) are exactly the case the next paragraph exists for: the capabilities handshake lights their buttons from the heartbeat, no dashboard deploy required — and play sharpened that rule into the dynamic verb passthrough: any heartbeat-advertised verb is invocable even before the dashboard knows its name, because a firmware-shipped verb must never again be visible-but-unsendable.

Since the capabilities pass, verb truth comes from the device itself: /api/capabilities crosses the dashboard's static table with the verbs the firmware advertises in its own heartbeat (first verified live at 15 verbs round-trip; the array has since grown to 19 — parity held, see Commands). A verb shipped by OTA lights its button without a dashboard deploy — the Sensors button staying grey for a day was exactly this staleness class. The semantics are honest in both directions: the device's word wins; unadvertised verbs grey out with the reason; verbs the firmware advertises that have no dedicated UI yet get a 🆕 chip pointing at the raw console; and if the platform is unreachable the static table takes over with the footer naming which source is speaking.

The verb console covers all of them with structured controls, not a free-text box: a nav ring for page (home/status/sensors/settings/wifi/ble + back/prev/next), a rotation control (0/90/180/270/auto/report, with the device's IMU answer read back), miccheck with a live/SILENT verdict badge parsed from the JSON reply, and sleep with timer-wake seconds. The console builds positional prompts for every sscanf-parsed verb — a lesson paid for on real glass: the first say implementation sent JSON and the panel dutifully rendered the literal braces. The screen mirror carries scroll controls (⤒ ▲ ▼) that drive the glass's own scroll verb and read back its pixel receipts (offset/content_h), refreshing the mirror after each step — scrolling the real panel from the browser, with the panel's own numbers as proof.

docs.title: Mock mode — the software Sticky
docs.text: STICKY_MOCK=1 (the default) swaps the relay for mock_device.py, which implements the device end of the envelope contract per the API contract — envelope dispatch, sleep-gating, help-on-unknown — and renders card specs to a real 800×480 PNG quantized to the 4 e-ink gray levels. It implements every verb, including the ones the firmware has not shipped, so it is the right target for UI work; a mock click is a real ui_tap because the mock device is the one being clicked.

docs.title: Auth lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Unclaimed: /auth/status → setup_required. First enrollment is gated by STICKY_AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN (the UI asks for it) so a public URL never has an open enrollment window — without the token, register/begin answers 403.
  2. Sealed: every /api/* route requires the session JWT (cookie or Authorization: Bearer); unauthenticated → 401. Additional passkeys can be added from a signed-in session; the last passkey cannot be deleted.
  3. Sessions last 24 h (STICKY_AUTH_TOKEN_TTL). A mid-session expiry is handled as one event: the first 401 on /api with a held token raises a single banner and the login gate — not a wall of failing cards.

Verified end-to-end with a CDP virtual authenticator (puppeteer + system Chrome): register → seal → invoke → clickable mirror tap → logout → passkey login, plus cookie-less 401/403 checks against the public URL.

docs.title: Cards
docs.text:
card source 📟 Device status — fw/battery/wifi/heap/display GET /api/status (both reply shapes), 30 s 🛰 Fleet row — name/id/kind/online/last seen GET /api/device → platform /api/devices, 60 s 🪞 Screen mirror — the real frame, clickable POST /api/screenshot → /api/screen.png + /api/buttons 🎨 render_ui composer — presets + JSON editor + live lint render_ui envelope (card spec v1) — the lint mirrors the firmware dispatch (7 types, keys, buttons≤4, priority), warns without blocking (the glass's receipt is the judge; only JSON parse errors block); presets include a scrollable 24-row list and an alert card. The lint is pinned to a declared grammar (LINT_GRAMMAR=2, stated next to the rules it mirrors), and status polls feed fwGrammar — the device is the only authority on what it speaks. On mismatch the Status card raises a ⚠ drift banner and every lint result confesses which version its rules mirror. The design proved itself the same night it shipped: grammar v2 (the messages dialect) reached the glass within hours of the pin landing, the banner fired unprompted on the first 0.14.11 poll, and the lint was then caught up — v2's real definition (verbs + button-id namespaces like m:, not card types) with the m: rows annotated. The Status row also shows fw_commit, so the panel can prove the deploy's ancestry at a glance ⚡ Actions — ask, voice ask, OTA (+greyed-out gaps) GET /api/capabilities decides what is clickable. The ota action carries a direction guard: a fresh status probe captures fw_before, the reply returns ota_guard{fw_before,note}, and staging opens a 30-minute watch: every parsed status receipt feeds the redeem, which logs the verdict itself — ⬆✅ upgraded, ⬆🚨 DOWNGRADED, ⌛ expired-unredeemed — receipts-based, because the channel pointer is device-token-auth'd and direction is provable only by evidence, not intent 💬 Messages — owner inbox, threads, unread badge, compose GET /api/messages (owner-side poll, 60 s); opening a thread (GET /api/messages/{peer}) is the explicit act that marks it read — and logs itself to the activity feed as dm_open, because a read-marking side effect should leave a trace. Sending is real: POST /api/messages delivers a DM through the owner relay (send_dm) — body capped at 2000 code points and rejected over-length, never truncated; an empty message is refused; the reply reports actual delivery (telegram/push/stored). Every send carries viaTiny provenance: a message composed by an agent or this dashboard must never claim a human typed it. 📟 deep-link buttons push the firmware's messages / messages thread <login> verbs — the same inbox or conversation appears on the physical glass, fetched by the device with its own token 📜 Activity — envelopes, replies, REAL ui_taps, sim_taps /api/activity ring + platform event ring, 5 s poll — entries render in receipt language (↕ scroll offsets in px, 🎨 committed-to-glass, ↩ late reply, ⌛ expired, ⏳ pending), and a ⬇ export button hands the whole session (receipts + in-flight) to another lane as timestamped JSON

The Sensors card exists now — but as an on-demand read, never a poll (each real read power-cycles the gyro, and a 30 s poll would spend the 750 mAh pack to decorate a dashboard). /api/sensors passes the firmware's JSON through verbatim — field names measured off tiny_sensors.cpp's emitters, not predicted — and the render is provenance-honest: gyro renders live dps when the read carries values (measured: it does), and a null gyro is explained as powered-down rather than dressed up as an error, absolute mAh appears only when mah_trusted is true, and an untrusted gauge is explained with its own numbers (design 7500 vs pack 750) rather than hidden. The card shows what the device knows and how much the device trusts what it knows.

docs.title: The HTTP surface
docs.text:
Every route in server.py, so integrators never have to read the cards table sideways. All /api/* routes require the session JWT (cookie or Bearer) except /api/health; /auth/* is the WebAuthn lifecycle.

route what it does GET /api/health unauthenticated liveness: mode (mock/live), device selector, whether first-passkey setup is still required GET /api/capabilities the device's own advertised verb list — what the UI is allowed to light up GET /api/device fleet row for the selected device via platform /api/devices GET /api/glass the glass-etiquette state as an API: busy + the open window's line + note (marquee markup stripped). The UI's 🚦 GlassBanner polls it every 15 s so a refused paint says why — which lane holds the announced window — instead of a mysterious 409. Etiquette that started as prose, became a gate (preflight_glass.py), and is now legible to every client POST /api/invoke raw verb → relay envelope; waits ≤ 45 s then returns {pending, envelope_id} (the use_device contract). Since the play premiere: any heartbeat-advertised verb passes through — the device's own word wins, the same rule the capabilities gate follows (a verb shipped in firmware was briefly visible-but-unsendable here because the dashboard kept its own allowlist; that contradiction is now structurally impossible). Scalar args flatten positionally for every verb, so a seq id never arrives JSON-quoted GET /api/result/{envelope_id} redeem a pending envelope later (relay mailbox keeps ~24 h) GET /api/status · GET /api/sensors normalized status (both reply shapes) · firmware sensor JSON passed through verbatim POST /api/screenshot → GET /api/screen.png trigger a framebuffer upload, then proxy the allowlisted media URL — the browser never sees it. Orientation travels with the pixels (owner ask): the response carries rotation + rotation_source (reply key → text fallback → an honest assumed 0), the mirror rotates its whole container so %-based tap zones stay glued to their pixels, and a ⟳ badge shows the effective rotation — the dashboard-side answer to the same runtime-state trap that white-painted the duck GET /api/buttons the tap zones of the last card, with bboxes, for the clickable mirror POST /api/tap simulated only, and it says so: refuses ids not on the last card sent from here (404), logs sim_tap with "the device did NOT feel this". Real ui_taps arrive the other way — device → platform event ring → activity feed GET /api/messages · GET /api/messages/{peer} · POST /api/messages inbox · thread (marks read, logs dm_open) · real DM send with the viaTiny provenance flag (see the Messages card row) GET /api/activity receipt-language feed + in_flight envelopes + upstream events_error when the platform pull is failing GET /auth/status · POST /auth/register/begin·finish · POST /auth/login/begin·finish · POST /auth/logout · GET·DELETE /auth/credentials passkey lifecycle — first enrollment gated by STICKY_AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN; the last passkey cannot be deleted POST /api/dither → GET /frames/{sha16}/{name} image rail: upload any image → dithered, exact-size raw e-ink frames + PNG previews. The GETs are capability URLs — sha16 of the content is the secret, no cookie — because the device fetches them over plain http_request with no cookie jar. Proven end-to-end in 0.19.0/M-A4: a rail frame rendered on the glass and screenshotted back diffed 0/384,000 pixels against the server's own preview. GET /api/dither returns the machine-readable contract (lesson learned: without it, the SPA catch-all served index.html and a firmware author would parse a web page as a spec) POST /api/frames → GET /api/frames/{seq_id}/{manifest,n.raw,n.png} anim rail (M-A8's backend half): anim-grammar JSON in (EINK_ANIMATION.md §4 — ops blit/rect/card_diff/delay/flush, canvas persists across ops, each paint op emits one frame) → Pillow rasterize → manifest + exact-size frames (0.raw = 48 000 B for 1-bit, receipt-verified) shaped for the firmware's tiny_stream_play(manifest_url, interval_s, max_frames) contract — a header-only declaration for one day (this page said so, citing what headers-without-implementation cost this repo), then implemented in 0.19.1 as the play verb: the rail rendered to the written contract, and the firmware's half arrived to meet a spec that already had receipts waiting. POST /api/frames/{seq_id}/play composes the whole path in one click — mirror the manifest + frames through the media host (cached, so a re-play doesn't re-upload) and send the play invoke; answers 501 when the firmware predates the verb rather than pretending. (The mirror was built as an allowlist bridge; the allowlist turned out not to exist — see the play correction, chapter 3. The route stays: cached media URLs are still the sturdier fetch target, and one click is one click.) The mirror itself is proven byte-identical (cmp: 48 000 B, IDENTICAL against the local rail); the duck still hasn't truly painted — take 2 reached the blit and painted white, since convicted as an unpinned rotation (the image card pins landscape, blit_1bit didn't; fixed in 0.19.4 — chapters 4–6). The formal M-A8 verdict rides the play status testimony. Caps enforced server-side and re-enforced on device (120 frames / 60 s; refusals carry the arithmetic). POST needs the session; the GETs are capability URLs like the image rail. GET /api/frames = public contract. The rail has four sources, all converging on the same validator → store → manifest → play path: hand-written anim-grammar JSON (above); POST /api/frames/prompt — "a ball bouncing left to right" → a Bedrock haiku turn taught the exact grammar, judged by the validator itself (one SpecError repair turn fed back verbatim, then an honest 422 carrying the last refusal; boto3/creds failures answer 502 with the name, never a blind 500); POST /api/frames/video — ffmpeg-sampled clip with the honest contract in the docstring: this is a time-lapse at e-ink cadence (≥250 ms/frame), never smooth motion — the panel physically cannot (long clips sample evenly across their duration rather than truncating); and the ANSI twin below GET /duck · GET /ansi/{seq_id} the terminal twin: any stored sequence replayed as chunked ANSI text (clear-screen + frame at manifest cadence, 60 s cap, cursor restored, signed off with one line). /ansi/{seq_id} is a capability URL exactly like the device's .raw fetches; /duck is the unauthenticated built-in demo — the marketing duck, rendered at server startup. It exists because a frame sequence you can curl is a frame sequence you can verify without touching the owner's glass — the ANSI twin is glass etiquette as infrastructure GET /api/settings · POST /api/settings/wifi · DELETE /api/settings/wifi/{ssid} · POST /api/settings/toggle remote settings rail (M-A9C) behind an honest capabilities gate: every write answers 409 with the gate sentence until the firmware advertises a config verb — the page never pretends a knob exists that the glass can't turn, and saved networks stay unlisted until config grows a get side (a gate sentence, never a fake list). Wi-Fi credentials ride a redacted invoke path: the password never enters the activity log, only a redacted line does GET /s/{device_id} scan-to-configure: the mobile page a QR on the glass points to. The page itself is public-shaped (holds no data); every API call it makes is WebAuthn-guarded, redirecting to enrollment/login client-side — the SPA shell's trust model, one URL hop from a QR scan GET /rtttl the piezo tune composer — a standalone client-side page (no build step): paste or compose RTTTL, hear it through a Web Audio square-wave oscillator that mimics the buzzer (corpus-accurate defaults d=4/o=6/b=63, dotted notes in both positions, 10 ms inter-note gaps), see it on a piano-roll canvas, start from 12 corpus presets. "Send to device" is deliberately disabled — the firmware has no chime/play verb yet (Commands → not in the firmware), and the dashboard does not invent relay verbs the glass never agreed to speak. The page exists so melodies are composed and auditioned before the engine ships, the same probe-before-build order the lockout used GET /{path} the built PWA (SPA fallback)

A vulnerability this table is honest about (found & fixed)

The SPA catch-all (GET /{path}) decoded %2e%2e before routing — an encoded-traversal request on the local port could read files beside the app, including .sticky_auth.json (the JWT secret). Found by the supervisor's route sweep while shipping /api/frames, fixed by containment (resolved paths must stay under dist/), and the jwt_secret was rotated — every session invalidated, passkeys kept. It's recorded here rather than buried because this page documents trust boundaries: capability URLs are only as good as the file server refusing to walk ...

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Four steps from a boxed reTerminal Sticky to me, alive on your fleet. I'll walk you through it. It's mostly waiting for a serial port.

Step zero: secure my way back

Before you touch my flash, read Recovery. A fresh unit deserves a full 32MB dump first — that dump is your unit's restore image, NVS and calibration included. My ROM bootloader survives any bad flash, so I'm unbrickable in practice — but only if you kept a way back.

docs.title: 0. Back up the factory brain (once, ~45 min)
docs.text:
My original firmware isn't bad, it's just not me. Save it:

pip install esptool                      # or: pipx install esptool
export STICKY_PORT=/dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX  # ls /dev/cu.usbmodem*  (Linux: /dev/ttyACM0)
# high baud rates fail through USB hub chains ("serial noise") — 115200 is the reliable one
esptool --port $STICKY_PORT read-flash 0 0x2000000 stock-firmware-32MB.bin
shasum -a 256 stock-firmware-32MB.bin > stock-firmware-32MB.bin.sha256

Yes, 45 minutes. I contain multitudes (32MB of them).

docs.title: 1. Build and flash
docs.text:
You need ESP-IDF v5.4 — the version my vendor HAL is tested against.

cd firmware
idf.py set-target esp32s3
idf.py build
idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbmodem5C843358881 flash monitor

After this, USB is only for emergencies. I update myself over the air — sha256-pinned, trial-boot, rollback armed. If a new build of me can't prove itself with a heartbeat, the old me comes back on its own.

docs.title: 2. Teach me your Wi-Fi
docs.text:
On first boot I have no token and no network, so I open a door: my glass shows a setup card with a QR code, and I broadcast an access point.

  1. Join tiny-XXXX (password tinysetup) — or just scan my QR, it encodes exactly that
  2. My portal lives at 192.168.4.1:
    • GET /info → who I am ({"kind":"reterminal-sticky", "provisioned":false, …})
    • POST /setup with {device_id, token, networks:[{ssid,key},…]}
    • GET / → a plain HTML form, the manual fallback
  3. I save everything to NVS and reboot onto your network

My portal is byte-compatible with the Nicla necklaces', so the tiny iOS app's "add device" flow onboards me with zero app changes. If my token is ever revoked, I reopen this door myself — three auth strikes, then the rescue portal, token kept for forensics. I never brick my own identity.

docs.title: 3. Enrollment
docs.text: The app side does this: POST /api/devices creates my row and mints the tind_… token the portal hands me. From then on I'm on duty — heartbeat every 30 seconds advertising what I can do, a poll for envelopes every 5.

docs.title: 4. Talk to me
docs.text:
From any tiny surface:

use_device invoke → prompt: "render_ui {\"type\":\"text\",\"title\":\"Dinner\",\"body\":\"Back at 19:30 — pizza in fridge\"}"
use_device invoke → prompt: "screenshot"
use_device invoke → prompt: "status"

Or skip the tooling entirely: press my AI button and ask by voice. Long-press is my home key.
